es.R: Así comenzó la buena noticia acerca de Jesús {{christos:Cristo|el Mesías}}.

fr.R: Voici comment a commencé la bonne nouvelle au sujet de Jésus {{christos:Christ|le Messie}}.

decisions.choice: a title: the opening words name what follows
alternatives: the first sentence of the story itself
decisions.reason: The line has no verb. It stands at the head of the book, or at least of its first part (1:2-13), and says where the good news begins: with John in the wilderness and Jesus' baptism.

decisions.choice: gospel: good news, the announcement of what God is doing
decisions.reason: The word means good news, used of a victory or a king's coming. Mark uses it for the message that Jesus proclaims (1:14-15). Only later did it become the name of a book.

decisions.choice: of Jesus Christ: the good news about him
alternatives: the good news that Jesus himself proclaimed
decisions.reason: Both are true in Mark, since Jesus proclaims the good news of God (1:14). Here, at the head of a story about him, Jesus is most likely the subject of the news.

decisions.choice: Christ: the Messiah, the anointed king God promised
decisions.reason: Christ is the Greek for the Hebrew Messiah, the anointed one. Israel's kings were anointed with oil, and the prophets promised a king from David's line. In Mark it is still a title (8:29; 14:61).

decisions.choice: the SBLGNT ends the line at Jesus Christ
decisions.reason: Many early and later manuscripts add "the Son of God", and Mark calls Jesus God's Son at key points (1:11; 15:39). A few early witnesses, including the first hand of Codex Sinaiticus, lack it. Scribes could have added the title, or dropped it by skipping a run of similar abbreviated words. Reviewers should check this against the SBLGNT apparatus.

decisions.choice: the gospel about Jesus (B); the good news about Jesus (R)
decisions.reason: "Of" could mean either, so Balanced and Readable say "about" to give the sense the meaning note prefers.

decisions.choice: "Tin Lành" for the gospel at every level, Readable included
decisions.reason: "Tin Lành" is the Protestant word and means "good news" in plain Vietnamese, so Readable needs no other word for what the English Readable calls "the good news"; Colossians uses it the same way. "Tin Mừng" is the Catholic word; "Phúc Âm" is older Sino-Vietnamese. Used through Mark.

decisions.choice: "Đức Giê-xu {{christos:Christ|Mê-si-a}}" with the name
decisions.reason: The style guide's form for Christ joined to the name; the honorific "Đức" is not bracketed even at Literal, since a bare name for Jesus is disrespectful in Vietnamese narrative.

decisions.choice: "복음" (L, B); "기쁜 소식" (R), through Mark
decisions.reason: "복음" is the established church word and is kept where the English says "gospel"; Readable uses the plain "기쁜 소식" (good news), as the English Readable and the Korean of Colossians do. The particle after the christos span ("의", "에 관한") fits both alternatives.

decisions.choice: evangelio (L, B); buena noticia (R)
decisions.reason: As for the English key term: Literal and Balanced keep the church word "evangelio"; Readable says "buena noticia", as the Spanish of 1 Peter and Colossians does. This applies throughout Mark.

decisions.choice: l’Évangile (L, B); la bonne nouvelle (R), for the whole book
decisions.reason: The noun follows the French already drafted for the letters (Colossians, 1 Peter): "l’Évangile" with a capital at Literal and Balanced, the message God sends, and "la bonne nouvelle" at Readable, which says what the word means (meaning decision m2). Balanced says "qui annonce Jésus" for the English "about Jesus" (meaning decision m3): "l’Évangile de Jésus" alone would read first as the gospel Jesus preached.

source.text: Καθὼς γέγραπται ἐν τῷ Ἠσαΐᾳ τῷ προφήτῃ· Ἰδοὺ ἀποστέλλω τὸν ἄγγελόν μου πρὸ προσώπου σου, ὃς κατασκευάσει τὴν ὁδόν σου·

records.literal_gloss: As it has been written in the Isaiah the prophet, Behold, I send the messenger of me before face of you, who will prepare the way of you;

en.L: Just as it has been written in Isaiah the prophet, "Look, I send {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} messenger before {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} face, who will prepare {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} way;
en.B: It happened just as it is written in the prophet Isaiah: "See, I am sending {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} messenger ahead of {{deity_pronoun:you|You}}; he will make {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} road ready.
en.R: Long ago God spoke through the prophet Isaiah. He said, "Look! I am sending {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} messenger ahead of {{deity_pronoun:you|You}}. He will get the road ready for {{deity_pronoun:you|You}}.

vi.L: Như đã được chép trong Ê-sai, nhà tiên tri: "Này, {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}} sai sứ giả của {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}} đi trước mặt Con, là người sẽ chuẩn bị con đường của Con;
vi.B: Việc ấy xảy ra đúng như lời đã chép trong sách tiên tri Ê-sai: "Này, {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}} sai sứ giả của {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}} đi trước Con; người ấy sẽ sửa soạn đường cho Con.
vi.R: Từ xưa, Đức Chúa Trời đã phán qua tiên tri Ê-sai: "Hãy xem! Ta sai sứ giả của {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}} đi trước Con. Người ấy sẽ dọn đường sẵn cho Con.

ko.L: 이사야 예언자의 [책에] 기록된 대로, "보아라, 내가 내 사자를 네 얼굴 앞에 보낸다. 그가 네 길을 마련할 것이다.
ko.B: 이사야 예언자의 글에 기록된 그대로 일이 이루어졌다. "보아라, 내가 내 사자를 너보다 앞서 보낸다. 그가 네 길을 닦아 놓을 것이다.
ko.R: 오래전에 하나님께서 이사야 예언자를 통해 말씀하셨다. "보아라! 내가 내 심부름꾼을 너보다 먼저 보낸다. 그가 너를 위해 길을 준비할 것이다.

es.L: Tal como está escrito en Isaías el profeta: «He aquí, envío a {{deity_pronoun:mi|Mi}} mensajero delante de {{deity_pronoun:tu|Tu}} rostro, el cual preparará {{deity_pronoun:tu|Tu}} camino;
es.B: Sucedió tal como está escrito en el profeta Isaías: «Mira, envío a {{deity_pronoun:mi|Mi}} mensajero delante de {{deity_pronoun:ti|Ti}}; él {{deity_pronoun:te|Te}} preparará el camino.
es.R: Hace mucho tiempo, Dios habló por medio del profeta Isaías. Dijo: «¡Mira! Envío a {{deity_pronoun:mi|Mi}} mensajero delante de {{deity_pronoun:ti|Ti}}. Él {{deity_pronoun:te|Te}} preparará el camino.

fr.L: Comme il a été écrit dans Isaïe le prophète : « Voici, j’envoie {{deity_pronoun:mon|Mon}} messager devant {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}} face, qui préparera {{deity_pronoun:ton|Ton}} chemin ;
fr.B: Tout arriva comme il est écrit chez le prophète Isaïe : « Regarde : j’envoie {{deity_pronoun:mon|Mon}} messager en avant de {{deity_pronoun:toi|Toi}} ; il {{deity_pronoun:te|Te}} préparera la route.
fr.R: Il y a longtemps, Dieu a parlé par le prophète Isaïe. Il a dit : « Regarde ! J’envoie {{deity_pronoun:mon|Mon}} messager devant {{deity_pronoun:toi|Toi}}. Il va préparer la route pour {{deity_pronoun:toi|Toi}}.

decisions.choice: the quotation joins Exodus 23:20 and Malachi 3:1 with Isaiah 40:3 (1:3)
decisions.reason: These words come from Exodus 23:20, where God sends his messenger before Israel, and Malachi 3:1, where the messenger prepares the way before the Lord. Mark joins them to Isaiah 40:3 and names Isaiah, the prophet of the road through the wilderness, for the whole.

decisions.choice: in Isaiah the prophet, the reading of the SBLGNT
decisions.reason: The oldest manuscripts name Isaiah. Many later ones read "in the prophets", most likely because scribes saw that the first lines come from elsewhere. Reviewers should check this against the SBLGNT apparatus.

decisions.choice: just as: the scripture is fulfilled in what follows, John's coming (1:4)
alternatives: just as: the scripture backs up the title in 1:1
decisions.reason: The sentence has no main verb of its own. It most likely leads into 1:4: John came just as it was written. It could also look back to 1:1, the beginning that scripture foretold.

decisions.choice: my: God speaks; you: the one who comes, Jesus; the messenger: John
decisions.reason: In Malachi the Lord says the messenger will prepare the way "before me". Here God speaks to another, "you", whose way John prepares. Mark tells the story so that this one is Jesus (1:9).

decisions.choice: my, your, you with deity_pronoun spans
decisions.reason: God speaks ("my") to the one whose way is prepared, Jesus ("your"), so the pronouns take the reader's capitalisation setting. "He" for the messenger is John and takes none.

decisions.choice: It happened just as (B); Long ago God spoke (R)
decisions.reason: An English sentence cannot begin with "just as" and stop. Balanced supplies "It happened", following the meaning note. Readable says that God is the speaker, as the first person "my" shows.

decisions.choice: God says "Ta" and speaks to the one who comes as "Con", capitalised, with no setting span
decisions.reason: Vietnamese must choose a relation for "you". The meaning decision says the one addressed is Jesus, whom the voice calls "Con" (Son) in 1:11; God speaking to Israel in Exodus 23:20 also speaks to his son (Exodus 4:22). "Ngài" is not how God addresses anyone, and "ngươi" is archaic and cold. A reviewer may prefer a less specific word.

decisions.choice: no deity_pronoun spans in Korean, through Mark 1; God speaks to the coming one in 해라체 ("내", "네", "너")
decisions.reason: Korean has no capital letters, so the setting has nothing to change; respect for God and Jesus is carried by "께서", "그분" and the honorific -시- at every level. In the quotation God speaks of himself and to the one who comes, so the plain style with no honorific is right, as a father speaks to a son.

decisions.choice: "이사야 예언자의 [책에]" (L); "사자" (L, B), "심부름꾼" (R)
decisions.reason: Korean cannot say "written in Isaiah" without a word for the book, so Literal brackets it. The Greek word for messenger can also mean angel, but here it is a human messenger (John); "사자" (envoy) is the standard word and Readable uses the everyday "심부름꾼".

decisions.choice: deity_pronoun spans on mi, tu, ti, te
alternatives: stressed pronouns only, as in John
decisions.reason: Book-wide rule for Mark in Spanish, following Romans and Hebrews: every pronoun Spanish writes for God or Christ takes the deity_pronoun setting, whether stressed (él, mí, ti), possessive (su, sus, mi, tu) or an object pronoun standing before the verb (lo, le, me, te). A subject that Spanish leaves in the verb ending has no pronoun to span; a pronoun at the start of a sentence is written plain, as English writes "He"; and a pronoun joined to the end of a verb ("síganme", "sígueme") cannot take the capital and stays plain, as in Colossians 3:5. The Spanish of John spans stressed pronouns only; a reviewer should settle one rule for the Gospels.

decisions.choice: He aquí (L); Mira (B, R)
decisions.reason: As in John 1:29: "he aquí" is formal but still current, so Literal keeps it; Balanced and Readable use the everyday word. The command is singular, spoken to the one who comes.

decisions.choice: mon (God speaking), ta, ton, toi, te (the one who comes) with deity_pronoun spans
decisions.reason: As in English (meaning decision m4): God speaks, and the one addressed is Jesus. French needs a span on the object pronoun "te" at Balanced, where English has none.

decisions.choice: Isaïe
decisions.reason: The form chosen for John 1:23 in French: "Isaïe" is the general French spelling, "Ésaïe" the Protestant one.

source.text: φωνὴ βοῶντος ἐν τῇ ἐρήμῳ· Ἑτοιμάσατε τὴν ὁδὸν κυρίου, εὐθείας ποιεῖτε τὰς τρίβους αὐτοῦ, ἐγένετο Ἰωάννης ὁ βαπτίζων ἐν τῇ ἐρήμῳ κηρύσσων βάπτισμα μετανοίας εἰς ἄφεσιν ἁμαρτιῶν.

records.literal_gloss: [The] voice of one crying in the wilderness, Prepare the way of [the] Lord, straight make the paths of him, \v 4 came John the [one] baptizing in the wilderness proclaiming a baptism of repentance for forgiveness of sins.

en.L: [the] voice of one crying out in the wilderness, 'Prepare the way of [the] Lord, make {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} paths straight,'" \v 4 John the Baptizer came in the wilderness, proclaiming a baptism of repentance for forgiveness of sins.
en.B: A voice is calling out in the wilderness: 'Prepare the way of the Lord, straighten the roads {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} will travel.'" \v 4 Then John the Baptizer came on the scene in the wilderness, calling people to a baptism of repentance for the forgiveness of their sins.
en.R: Someone is shouting in the desert: 'Get the road ready for the Lord! Make {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} paths straight!'" \v 4 That messenger was John the Baptizer. He came to the desert and told people to turn away from their sins and be baptized, so that God would forgive them.

vi.L: tiếng của [người] kêu lên trong đồng hoang: 'Hãy dọn đường của Chúa, hãy làm cho thẳng các lối của {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}},'" \v 4 Giăng, người làm báp-têm, đã xuất hiện trong đồng hoang, rao giảng phép báp-têm của sự ăn năn để được tha tội.
vi.B: Có tiếng kêu lên trong đồng hoang: 'Hãy dọn đường cho Chúa, hãy sửa cho thẳng những lối {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} sẽ đi.'" \v 4 Rồi Giăng Báp-tít xuất hiện trong đồng hoang, kêu gọi người ta chịu báp-têm để bày tỏ sự ăn năn, hầu được tha tội.
vi.R: Có người đang kêu lớn trong sa mạc: 'Hãy dọn đường sẵn cho Chúa! Hãy làm thẳng các lối {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} đi!'" \v 4 Sứ giả ấy là Giăng Báp-tít. Ông đến sa mạc và bảo người ta hãy từ bỏ tội lỗi, quay về với Đức Chúa Trời và chịu báp-têm, để Đức Chúa Trời tha tội cho họ.

ko.L: 광야에서 외치는 사람의 소리[가 들린다]. '주님의 길을 준비하여라. 그분의 오솔길들을 곧게 만들어라.'" \v 4 세례를 주는 요한이 광야에 나타나서, 죄 용서에 이르는 회개의 세례를 선포하였다.
ko.B: 광야에서 외치는 사람의 소리가 있다. '주님의 길을 준비하여라. 그분이 다니실 길을 곧게 내어라.'" \v 4 그리고 세례자 요한이 광야에 나타나서, 사람들에게 회개의 세례를 받아 죄를 용서받으라고 선포했다.
ko.R: 빈 들에서 누군가가 외치고 있다. '주님께서 오실 길을 준비하여라! 그분이 다니실 길을 곧게 만들어라!'" \v 4 그 심부름꾼이 바로 세례자 요한이었다. 요한은 빈 들에 와서 사람들에게 죄에서 돌이켜 세례를 받으라고 말했다. 그러면 하나님께서 그들의 죄를 용서해 주실 것이라고 했다.

es.L: voz de uno que clama en el desierto: “{{plural_you:Preparen|Preparad}} el camino del Señor, {{plural_you:hagan|haced}} rectas {{deity_pronoun:sus|Sus}} sendas”». \v 4 Apareció Juan, el que bautizaba, en el desierto, proclamando un bautismo de arrepentimiento para perdón de pecados.
es.B: Una voz clama en el desierto: “{{plural_you:Preparen|Preparad}} el camino del Señor; {{plural_you:enderecen|enderezad}} las sendas por donde ha de pasar”». \v 4 Entonces apareció en el desierto Juan el Bautista, llamando a la gente a un bautismo de arrepentimiento para el perdón de sus pecados.
es.R: Alguien grita en el desierto: “¡{{plural_you:Preparen|Preparad}} el camino para el Señor! ¡{{plural_you:Hagan|Haced}} rectas {{deity_pronoun:sus|Sus}} sendas!”». \v 4 Ese mensajero era Juan el Bautista. Llegó al desierto y le decía a la gente que se apartara de sus pecados y se bautizara, para que Dios la perdonara.

fr.L: [une] voix de [quelqu’un] criant dans le désert : “Préparez le chemin du Seigneur, rendez droits {{deity_pronoun:ses|Ses}} sentiers.” » \v 4 Jean le Baptiseur parut dans le désert, proclamant un baptême de repentance pour [le] pardon des péchés.
fr.B: Une voix crie dans le désert : “Préparez le chemin du Seigneur, tracez droites les routes où {{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} passera.” » \v 4 Alors Jean le Baptiseur parut dans le désert ; il appelait les gens à se faire baptiser en signe de repentance, pour que leurs péchés soient pardonnés.
fr.R: Quelqu’un crie dans le désert : “Préparez la route pour le Seigneur ! Faites-{{deity_pronoun:lui|Lui}} des chemins bien droits !” » \v 4 Ce messager, c’était Jean le Baptiseur. Il est venu dans le désert et il disait aux gens de se détourner de leurs péchés et de se faire baptiser, pour que Dieu leur pardonne.

decisions.choice: Isaiah 40:3: the voice that prepares the Lord's road home
decisions.reason: In Isaiah a voice calls for a road through the wilderness, so that God can lead his people home from exile. The wilderness is where John appears (1:4).

decisions.choice: the Lord: God in Isaiah; the one John prepares for is Jesus
decisions.reason: In Isaiah the Lord is God himself, the divine name. Mark sets the words so that the one whose road is made ready is Jesus, who comes in 1:9.

decisions.choice: the Baptizer: a title, the one who baptizes
alternatives: John, who was baptizing in the wilderness
decisions.reason: With the article the participle is a name for John, as in 6:14 and 6:24. Many manuscripts lack the article or add "and" before "proclaiming", which makes it a description of what John was doing.

decisions.choice: a baptism of repentance: a washing that marked a turning back to God
alternatives: a baptism that itself made people repent
decisions.reason: Repentance is a change of mind and of the whole way of life (see 1:15). Being dipped in the river showed that a person had turned back to God.

decisions.choice: for forgiveness of sins: leading to forgiveness, which God gives
alternatives: because sins had already been forgiven
decisions.reason: The word "for" points to the goal: the people who turned back would be forgiven. Forgiving sins belongs to God (2:7).

decisions.choice: the Baptizer
decisions.reason: Mark's word here is "the one who baptizes", not the noun Matthew uses (Matthew 3:1). "Baptizer" keeps the difference, which the meaning note explains.

decisions.choice: That messenger was John the Baptizer.
decisions.reason: Readable says plainly what the quotation and the story imply, that John is the messenger and the voice of 1:2-3.

decisions.choice: "Giăng, người làm báp-têm" (L); "Giăng Báp-tít" (B, R)
decisions.reason: The Greek is a participle, "the one baptizing", and Literal shows it. Balanced and Readable use the title Protestant readers know, which says the same thing; "Tẩy Giả" is the Catholic form.

decisions.choice: "sự ăn năn", "được tha tội" (L, B); "từ bỏ tội lỗi, quay về với Đức Chúa Trời" (R)
decisions.reason: "ăn năn" is the Protestant word for repentance and is used for the verb in 1:15 too; "sám hối" has a Buddhist and Catholic ring. Readable unfolds the word as the English Readable does.

decisions.choice: "đồng hoang" (L, B); "sa mạc" (R)
decisions.reason: As in John 1:23: "đồng hoang" is the modern word for empty, uninhabited land; Readable uses the commoner "sa mạc", as the English Readable says "desert". Kept for the wilderness through 1:13 and echoed in "nơi hoang vắng" (1:35, 1:45).

decisions.choice: "세례를 주는 요한" (L); "세례자 요한" (B, R)
decisions.reason: The Greek is a participle used as a title (meaning decision). Literal keeps the participle; Balanced and Readable use the modern title "세례자". "세례 요한" is the older familiar form; "침례" belongs to one church tradition.

decisions.choice: "광야" (L, B), "빈 들" (R); "주님" for the Lord
decisions.reason: As in John 1:23: "광야" is the established word for the wilderness of Isaiah 40:3 and of Israel's testing; Readable uses the plain native "빈 들" rather than "사막" (sandy desert). "주님" is the current respectful word for the Lord, here God, as the meaning decision says.

decisions.choice: "회개" (L, B); "죄에서 돌이켜" (R), through Mark
decisions.reason: "회개" is the established word and keeps the link with 1:15 and 6:12; it can sound like mere regret to new readers, so Readable says what it means, turning from sin back to God, as the English Readable does in 1:15.

decisions.choice: el que bautizaba (L); el Bautista (B, R)
decisions.reason: Mark calls John "the one baptizing", used as a title (meaning decision m3). Literal shows the participle; Balanced and Readable use the title Spanish readers know, which says the same thing.

decisions.choice: ustedes / vosotros forms; « » outside, “ ” inside
decisions.reason: Plural "you" takes the reader setting: ustedes (Latin America, the default) or vosotros (Spain), here and throughout Mark. The quotation opens with « in 1:2 and closes here; the quotation from Isaiah inside it takes “ ”, as in John.

decisions.choice: Tenses for Mark 1: Literal keeps the Greek tenses (Mark's historic present "ils entrent", "il dit"; the imperfect for what went on; the passé simple for the aorists); Balanced narrates in the passé simple ("parut", "vint") with the imperfect for description and the passé composé in speech; Readable uses the passé composé and imperfect throughout ("il est venu", "il disait")
decisions.reason: The French brief, recorded once for the chapter, as for John. The passé simple is the normal tense of written French narrative and suits a public reading; young readers meet narrative mostly in the passé composé, so Readable has no passé simple. Mark's historic presents are kept only at Literal, where they show the Greek form.

decisions.choice: Jean le Baptiseur
decisions.reason: The Greek here is a participle used as a title, "the one who baptizes" (meaning decision m3), and English says "the Baptizer". "Baptiseur" says the same in French and keeps the link with the verb "baptiser" that follows; "Jean-Baptiste", the familiar French name, reads as a proper name. Mark also uses the noun form (6:25; 8:28), which may be rendered "le Baptiste" there.

decisions.choice: le désert, at every level (also 1:4, 1:12-13; un lieu désert, des lieux déserts in 1:35, 1:45)
decisions.reason: French "désert" covers the Greek word's range, empty land where no one lives, so one word can stand at every level where English varies between "wilderness" and "desert". It keeps the link the meaning decisions point out between Isaiah's voice, John, Jesus's testing and the lonely places he goes to pray (1:35, 1:45).

source.text: καὶ ἐξεπορεύετο πρὸς αὐτὸν πᾶσα ἡ Ἰουδαία χώρα καὶ οἱ Ἱεροσολυμῖται πάντες, καὶ ἐβαπτίζοντο ὑπ’ αὐτοῦ ἐν τῷ Ἰορδάνῃ ποταμῷ ἐξομολογούμενοι τὰς ἁμαρτίας αὐτῶν.

records.literal_gloss: And were going out to him all the Judean region and the Jerusalemites all, and were being baptized by him in the Jordan river, confessing the sins of them.

en.L: And all the Judean region and all the people of Jerusalem were going out to him, and they were being baptized by him in the Jordan River, confessing their sins.
en.B: The whole land of Judea and everyone from Jerusalem kept going out to him. They confessed their sins, and he baptized them in the Jordan River.
en.R: People came to him from everywhere in Judea and from the city of Jerusalem. They told God the wrong things they had done, and John baptized them in the Jordan River.

vi.L: Và cả xứ Giu-đê và hết thảy dân Giê-ru-sa-lem đều kéo ra với ông, và họ được ông làm báp-têm trong sông Giô-đanh, xưng tội mình.
vi.B: Cả xứ Giu-đê và toàn dân Giê-ru-sa-lem lũ lượt kéo ra với ông. Họ xưng tội mình và được ông làm báp-têm dưới sông Giô-đanh.
vi.R: Người ta từ khắp miền Giu-đê và từ thành Giê-ru-sa-lem kéo đến với ông. Họ thú nhận với Đức Chúa Trời những điều sai trái mình đã làm, và Giăng làm báp-têm cho họ dưới sông Giô-đanh.

ko.L: 그리고 온 유대 지방과 모든 예루살렘 사람들이 그에게로 나가고 있었고, 자기들의 죄를 고백하며 요단강에서 그에게 세례를 받고 있었다.
ko.B: 온 유대 지방과 예루살렘의 모든 사람들이 줄지어 요한에게로 나왔다. 그들은 자기 죄를 고백했고, 요한은 요단강에서 그들에게 세례를 주었다.
ko.R: 유대 온 지역과 예루살렘 성에서 사람들이 요한에게 몰려왔다. 그들은 자기가 저지른 잘못을 하나님께 털어놓았고, 요한은 요단강에서 그들에게 세례를 주었다.

es.L: Y salían hacia él toda la región de Judea y todos los de Jerusalén, y eran bautizados por él en el río Jordán, confesando sus pecados.
es.B: Toda la región de Judea y toda la gente de Jerusalén acudían a él. Confesaban sus pecados, y él los bautizaba en el río Jordán.
es.R: Gente de toda Judea y de la ciudad de Jerusalén venía a verlo. Le contaban a Dios las cosas malas que habían hecho, y Juan los bautizaba en el río Jordán.

fr.L: Et toute la région de Judée et tous les habitants de Jérusalem sortaient vers lui, et ils étaient baptisés par lui dans le fleuve Jourdain, en confessant leurs péchés.
fr.B: Tout le pays de Judée et tous les habitants de Jérusalem venaient à lui. Ils confessaient leurs péchés, et il les baptisait dans le Jourdain.
fr.R: Des gens venaient le voir de partout en Judée et de la ville de Jérusalem. Ils disaient à Dieu le mal qu’ils avaient fait, et Jean les baptisait dans le Jourdain.

decisions.choice: all: a great many, the whole region in motion
decisions.reason: "All" stresses how many came, as people speak of a whole town turning out. Mark later says that the leaders did not accept John (11:30-31).

decisions.choice: were going out, were being baptized: a stream of people over time
alternatives: a single crowd on one day
decisions.reason: The verbs are continuous: people kept coming and being baptized.

decisions.choice: confessing: openly admitting their sins
decisions.reason: The word means to agree openly, to say out loud. Here it is the sins that are owned up to.

decisions.choice: the Jordan River: the river running from the Sea of Galilee to the Dead Sea
alternatives: a pool or stream near Jerusalem
decisions.reason: The Jordan was the border Israel crossed to enter the promised land (Joshua 3). John baptized in the wilderness stretch near Jericho.

decisions.choice: told God the wrong things they had done
decisions.reason: Readable says what confessing sins means in plain words. Confession was made before God, and the crowd heard it.

decisions.choice: "그에게 세례를 받고 있었다" for "were being baptized by him"
decisions.reason: Korean expresses this passive with "세례를 받다" (receive baptism) and "에게"; "에 의해" is a translation calque. The imperfect "-고 있었다" keeps the stream of people the meaning decision describes.

decisions.choice: toute la région de Judée et tous les habitants de Jérusalem ... sortaient
decisions.reason: French puts the long subject before the verb; Literal keeps the Greek imperfects ("sortaient", "étaient baptisés"), which describe a stream of people over time (meaning decision m2).

source.text: καὶ ἦν ὁ Ἰωάννης ἐνδεδυμένος τρίχας καμήλου καὶ ζώνην δερματίνην περὶ τὴν ὀσφὺν αὐτοῦ, καὶ ἔσθων ἀκρίδας καὶ μέλι ἄγριον.

records.literal_gloss: And was the John clothed [in] hair of camel and a belt leathern around the waist of him, and eating locusts and honey wild.

en.L: And John was clothed [in] camel's hair and [had] a leather belt around his waist, and [he was] eating locusts and wild honey.
en.B: John's clothes were made of camel's hair, and he had a leather belt around his waist. He lived on locusts and wild honey.
en.R: John wore clothes made from camel hair, with a leather belt around his waist. He ate locusts, a kind of grasshopper, and honey that he found in the wild.

vi.L: Và Giăng mặc [áo bằng] lông lạc đà và [có] dây thắt lưng bằng da quanh hông, và ăn châu chấu và mật ong rừng.
vi.B: Giăng mặc áo bằng lông lạc đà, thắt lưng bằng dây da. Ông sống bằng châu chấu và mật ong rừng.
vi.R: Giăng mặc áo làm bằng lông lạc đà, có dây da thắt ngang lưng. Ông ăn châu chấu và mật ong tìm được ngoài hoang dã.

ko.L: 그리고 요한은 낙타 털 [옷을] 입고 허리에 가죽 띠를 [두르고] 있었으며, 메뚜기와 들꿀을 먹고 있었다.
ko.B: 요한은 낙타 털로 만든 옷을 입고 허리에 가죽 띠를 둘렀다. 그는 메뚜기와 들꿀을 먹고 살았다.
ko.R: 요한은 낙타 털로 만든 옷을 입고, 허리에는 가죽 띠를 매고 있었다. 그는 메뚜기와 들에서 찾은 꿀을 먹었다.

es.L: Y Juan estaba vestido [de] pelo de camello y [llevaba] un cinturón de cuero alrededor de su cintura, y comía langostas y miel silvestre.
es.B: Juan llevaba ropa hecha de pelo de camello y un cinturón de cuero en la cintura. Se alimentaba de langostas y miel silvestre.
es.R: Juan se vestía con ropa de pelo de camello y llevaba un cinturón de cuero en la cintura. Comía langostas, que son una especie de saltamontes, y miel que encontraba en el campo.

fr.L: Et Jean était vêtu de poils de chameau, et [il avait] une ceinture de cuir autour de la taille, et [il] mangeait des sauterelles et du miel sauvage.
fr.B: Jean portait un vêtement de poils de chameau et une ceinture de cuir autour de la taille. Il se nourrissait de sauterelles et de miel sauvage.
fr.R: Jean portait des habits faits en poils de chameau, avec une ceinture de cuir autour de la taille. Il mangeait des sauterelles, une sorte de gros criquets, et du miel qu’il trouvait dans la nature.

decisions.choice: camel's hair and a leather belt: the dress of Elijah
alternatives: simply the clothing of a poor man
decisions.reason: Elijah is described as a hairy man with a leather belt around his waist (2 Kings 1:8). Malachi 4:5 promised that Elijah would come before the day of the Lord, and Jesus later says that he has come (9:13).

decisions.choice: locusts and wild honey: food found in the wilderness
alternatives: a special diet for a vow
decisions.reason: Locusts were clean food under the law (Leviticus 11:22), and wild bees' honey could be found in rocks and trees. John lived on what the wilderness gave.

decisions.choice: locusts, a kind of grasshopper
decisions.reason: Many readers do not know that a locust is an insect, so Readable says so, as in Matthew 3:4.

decisions.choice: "châu chấu" with no explanation (R)
decisions.reason: The English Readable explains "locusts"; "châu chấu" is an everyday Vietnamese word, and locusts are still eaten in parts of Vietnam, so no explanation is needed.

decisions.choice: "메뚜기" with no explanation (R)
decisions.reason: The English Readable explains "locusts" as a kind of grasshopper; the everyday Korean word "메뚜기" already covers both, so no explanation is needed.

decisions.choice: [de], [llevaba]
decisions.reason: Spanish needs a preposition after "vestido" and a verb for the belt, which the Greek leaves to the one participle "clothed".

decisions.choice: [il avait], [il]
decisions.reason: French needs a verb and a subject that the Greek participles leave out, so Literal brackets them.

source.text: καὶ ἐκήρυσσεν λέγων· Ἔρχεται ὁ ἰσχυρότερός μου ὀπίσω μου, οὗ οὐκ εἰμὶ ἱκανὸς κύψας λῦσαι τὸν ἱμάντα τῶν ὑποδημάτων αὐτοῦ·

records.literal_gloss: And he was proclaiming saying, Comes the [one] mightier [than] me after me, of whom not I am worthy having stooped down to untie the strap of the sandals of him.

en.L: And he was proclaiming, saying, "One mightier than I is coming after me; I am not fit to stoop down [and] untie the strap of {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} sandals.
en.B: This was his message: "Someone stronger than I am is coming after me. I am not fit even to bend down and untie the strap of {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} sandals.
en.R: He told the people, "Someone much greater than I am is coming after me. I am not good enough even to bend down and untie {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} sandals.

vi.L: Và ông rao giảng rằng: "Đấng quyền năng hơn tôi đến sau tôi; tôi không xứng đáng cúi xuống mở quai dép của {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}}.
vi.B: Ông rao giảng: "Có Đấng quyền năng hơn tôi đang đến sau tôi. Tôi không đáng cúi xuống cởi quai dép cho {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}}.
vi.R: Ông nói với dân chúng: "Có một Đấng lớn hơn tôi rất nhiều sẽ đến sau tôi. Tôi không xứng đáng ngay cả cúi xuống cởi dép cho {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}}.

ko.L: 그리고 그는 선포하며 말하였다. "나보다 더 강하신 분이 내 뒤에 오신다. 나는 몸을 굽혀 그분의 신발 끈을 풀 자격도 없다.
ko.B: 요한이 선포한 말은 이러했다. "나보다 더 능력 있는 분이 내 뒤에 오신다. 나는 몸을 굽혀 그분의 신발 끈을 풀어 드릴 자격조차 없다.
ko.R: 요한은 사람들에게 이렇게 전했다. "나보다 훨씬 더 크신 분이 내 뒤에 오신다. 나는 몸을 굽혀 그분의 신발을 벗겨 드릴 만한 사람도 못 된다.

es.L: Y proclamaba, diciendo: «Viene después de mí el que es más fuerte que yo, de quien no soy digno de agacharme a desatar la correa de {{deity_pronoun:sus|Sus}} sandalias.
es.B: Este era su mensaje: «Después de mí viene uno más fuerte que yo. Yo no soy quién para agacharme a desatar la correa de {{deity_pronoun:sus|Sus}} sandalias.
es.R: Le decía a la gente: «Después de mí viene alguien mucho más importante que yo. Yo no valgo ni siquiera para agacharme a desatar {{deity_pronoun:sus|Sus}} sandalias.

fr.L: Et il proclamait, disant : « Il vient après moi, celui qui est plus fort que moi ; je ne suis pas digne de me baisser [pour] délier la courroie de {{deity_pronoun:ses|Ses}} sandales.
fr.B: Voici ce qu’il annonçait : « Quelqu’un de plus fort que moi vient après moi. Je ne mérite même pas de me baisser pour dénouer la lanière de {{deity_pronoun:ses|Ses}} sandales.
fr.R: Il disait aux gens : « Quelqu’un de beaucoup plus grand que moi va venir après moi. Je ne suis même pas assez important pour me baisser et détacher {{deity_pronoun:ses|Ses}} sandales.

decisions.choice: the one coming after me: the Messiah, whom John does not name
decisions.reason: John points away from himself to one greater, who will baptize with the Holy Spirit (1:8). Mark's next scene shows who it is (1:9-11).

decisions.choice: untie his sandals: the task of the lowest slave
decisions.reason: Taking off a master's sandals was a slave's job. John says he is not fit to do even that for the one who is coming.

decisions.choice: after me: later in time
decisions.reason: The words can mean "behind", as a disciple follows a teacher, but here they mean that the mightier one comes after John's work.

decisions.choice: not fit
decisions.reason: The word means sufficient or fit for a task, and Matthew 3:11 uses "fit" for the same saying.

decisions.choice: John preaches to the crowds in 해라체 ("오신다", "없다", "너희") and speaks of the coming one with the honorific ("강하신 분", "오신다", "그분")
alternatives: 합쇼체 with "여러분", as John speaks to the envoys in John 1:26
decisions.reason: A prophet proclaiming to the crowds speaks plainly, as Jesus does; in John 1:26 John answers an official delegation, which is a different scene. The one who comes is the Messiah, so John refers to him with the honorific, as in John 1:27-30.

decisions.choice: "선포하다" (L, B), "전하다" (R), for the verb of proclaiming, through Mark
decisions.reason: "선포하다" (proclaim, announce publicly) keeps the herald's announcement that the Greek word names, and links John, Jesus and the healed man (1:4, 1:14, 1:38-39, 1:45). "전파하다" is older church language; "설교하다" suggests a sermon in church. Readable uses the plain "전하다" (tell, pass on).

decisions.choice: no soy digno (L); no soy quién para (B); no valgo ni siquiera para (R)
decisions.reason: The Greek word means fit or good enough for a task. Literal uses the usual Spanish "digno"; Balanced and Readable use everyday idioms for not being good enough to do something.

decisions.choice: después de mí
decisions.reason: Meaning decision m3 takes "after me" as later in time, so every level says "después de mí" rather than "detrás de mí", which in Spanish is first heard as a place.

decisions.choice: je ne suis pas digne (L); je ne mérite même pas (B); je ne suis même pas assez important (R)
decisions.reason: The Greek word means "fit, good enough" for the task. French says this with "digne" or "mériter"; "capable" or "qualifié" would suggest a lack of skill, not of standing.

source.text: ἐγὼ ἐβάπτισα ὑμᾶς ὕδατι, αὐτὸς δὲ βαπτίσει ὑμᾶς ἐν πνεύματι ἁγίῳ.

records.literal_gloss: I baptized you with water, he but will baptize you in [the] Spirit Holy.

en.L: I baptized you with water, but {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} will baptize you in [the] Holy Spirit."
en.B: The baptism I gave you was with water; {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} will baptize you with the Holy Spirit."
en.R: I used water when I baptized you. But {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} will baptize you with the Holy Spirit."

vi.L: Tôi đã làm báp-têm cho các người bằng nước, nhưng {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} sẽ làm báp-têm cho các người trong Đức Thánh Linh."
vi.B: Tôi làm báp-têm cho các người bằng nước, nhưng {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} sẽ làm báp-têm cho các người bằng Đức Thánh Linh."
vi.R: Tôi dùng nước để làm báp-têm cho các người. Nhưng {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} sẽ làm báp-têm cho các người bằng Đức Thánh Linh."

ko.L: 나는 너희에게 물로 세례를 주었지만, 그분은 너희에게 성령으로 세례를 주실 것이다."
ko.B: 나는 너희에게 물로 세례를 주었다. 그러나 그분은 성령으로 너희에게 세례를 주실 것이다."
ko.R: 나는 너희에게 세례를 줄 때 물을 썼다. 그러나 그분은 성령으로 너희에게 세례를 주실 것이다."

es.L: Yo {{plural_you:los|os}} bauticé con agua, pero {{deity_pronoun:él|Él}} {{plural_you:los|os}} bautizará en [el] Espíritu Santo».
es.B: Yo {{plural_you:los|os}} he bautizado con agua, pero {{deity_pronoun:él|Él}} {{plural_you:los|os}} bautizará con el Espíritu Santo».
es.R: Yo {{plural_you:los|os}} bauticé con agua. Pero {{deity_pronoun:él|Él}} {{plural_you:los|os}} bautizará con el Espíritu Santo».

fr.L: Moi, je vous ai baptisés d’eau, mais {{deity_pronoun:lui|Lui}}, {{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} vous baptisera dans [l’]Esprit Saint. »
fr.B: Moi, je vous ai baptisés avec de l’eau ; {{deity_pronoun:lui|Lui}} vous baptisera avec l’Esprit Saint. »
fr.R: Moi, je vous ai baptisés avec de l’eau. Mais {{deity_pronoun:lui|Lui}}, {{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} vous baptisera avec l’Esprit Saint. »

decisions.choice: I baptized: John looks at the work he has done
decisions.reason: The verb is past. John speaks of his baptism as done, set against what the coming one will do.

decisions.choice: baptize with the Holy Spirit: pour out God's Spirit on people
decisions.reason: The prophets promised that God would pour out his Spirit on his people (Joel 2:28; Ezekiel 36:26-27). The one who is coming will do what water only pictures.

decisions.choice: in the Spirit: the Spirit is what people will be plunged into
alternatives: by the Spirit, as the one who acts
decisions.reason: Water and the Spirit stand side by side as the element of each baptism.

decisions.choice: with water, in the Holy Spirit (L); with ... with (B, R)
alternatives: in water, in the Holy Spirit
decisions.reason: The Greek has no preposition with "water" and "in" with "Spirit". Literal keeps the difference. Balanced and Readable say "with" for both, the natural English.

decisions.choice: John speaks to the crowds as "các người"
decisions.reason: A prophet addressing the whole crowd, men and women, speaks as the style guide has Jesus speak to crowds; "các ông" (used to the envoys in John 1:19-27) would address only men.

decisions.choice: "물로" and "성령으로" at every level
decisions.reason: Korean "-로 세례를 주다" covers both "with" and "in", as in John 1:26 and 1:33; "성령 안에서" would sound as if the Spirit were the place where the baptizer stands. The English Literal's "in" has no natural Korean counterpart; the meaning decision explains the picture of being plunged into the Spirit.

decisions.choice: dans [l’]Esprit Saint
decisions.reason: The Greek has no article and French cannot leave it out, so Literal brackets it, as in John 1:33. "Moi ... lui, il" shows the emphatic pronouns of the Greek.

source.text: Καὶ ἐγένετο ἐν ἐκείναις ταῖς ἡμέραις ἦλθεν Ἰησοῦς ἀπὸ Ναζαρὲτ τῆς Γαλιλαίας καὶ ἐβαπτίσθη εἰς τὸν Ἰορδάνην ὑπὸ Ἰωάννου.

records.literal_gloss: And it came to pass in those the days came Jesus from Nazareth of the Galilee and was baptized into the Jordan by John.

en.L: And it happened in those days [that] Jesus came from Nazareth of Galilee and was baptized into the Jordan by John.
en.B: It was during those days that Jesus came from Nazareth in Galilee, and John baptized {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} in the Jordan.
en.R: During that time, Jesus came from the town of Nazareth in the land of Galilee. John baptized {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} in the Jordan River.

vi.L: Và xảy ra trong những ngày ấy, Đức Giê-xu từ Na-xa-rét thuộc Ga-li-lê đến và được Giăng làm báp-têm trong sông Giô-đanh.
vi.B: Trong những ngày ấy, Đức Giê-xu từ Na-xa-rét, xứ Ga-li-lê, đến và được Giăng làm báp-têm dưới sông Giô-đanh.
vi.R: Trong thời gian đó, Đức Giê-xu từ làng Na-xa-rét ở miền Ga-li-lê đến. Giăng làm báp-têm cho {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} dưới sông Giô-đanh.

ko.L: 그리고 그 날들에 [이런] 일이 있었다. 예수께서 갈릴리의 나사렛에서 오셔서, 요단강에 [들어가] 요한에게 세례를 받으셨다.
ko.B: 그 무렵에 예수께서 갈릴리 나사렛에서 오셔서 요단강에서 요한에게 세례를 받으셨다.
ko.R: 그때 예수께서 갈릴리 지방의 나사렛 마을에서 오셨다. 그리고 요단강에서 요한에게 세례를 받으셨다.

es.L: Y sucedió en aquellos días [que] vino Jesús desde Nazaret de Galilea y fue bautizado en el Jordán por Juan.
es.B: Por aquellos días, Jesús llegó desde Nazaret, en Galilea, y Juan {{deity_pronoun:lo|Lo}} bautizó en el Jordán.
es.R: En ese tiempo, Jesús vino desde el pueblo de Nazaret, en la región de Galilea. Juan {{deity_pronoun:lo|Lo}} bautizó en el río Jordán.

fr.L: Et il arriva en ces jours-là [que] Jésus vint de Nazareth de Galilée et fut baptisé dans le Jourdain par Jean.
fr.B: En ces jours-là, Jésus vint de Nazareth, en Galilée, et Jean {{deity_pronoun:le|Le}} baptisa dans le Jourdain.
fr.R: À cette époque, Jésus est venu de Nazareth, un village de Galilée. Jean {{deity_pronoun:l’|L’}}a baptisé dans le Jourdain.

decisions.choice: it happened: the old biblical way of starting a new event
decisions.reason: The phrase follows the style of the Greek Old Testament and simply opens a new scene.

decisions.choice: Nazareth of Galilee: a small village in the hills of Galilee
decisions.reason: Nazareth is not named in the Old Testament and was an unimportant place (John 1:46). Galilee was the northern region, far from Jerusalem.

decisions.choice: into the Jordan: Jesus went down into the river
alternatives: at the Jordan, on the bank
decisions.reason: "Into" pictures him being dipped in the water. He comes up out of it in 1:10.

decisions.choice: it happened (L only); John baptized him (B, R)
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable leave out the old opening phrase and make John the subject, which reads more naturally.

decisions.choice: Jesus stays the subject at every level: "요한에게 세례를 받으셨다"
alternatives: "요한이 예수께 세례를 주었다" (B, R), as the English
decisions.reason: The English Balanced and Readable make John the subject; Korean says "received baptism from John" naturally, and keeping Jesus as the subject keeps the honorific -시- on the main verb of the sentence.

decisions.choice: "요단강에 [들어가]" (L)
decisions.reason: The Greek "into the Jordan" implies going down into the river (meaning decision); Korean needs a verb for the movement, which Literal brackets.

source.text: καὶ εὐθὺς ἀναβαίνων ἐκ τοῦ ὕδατος εἶδεν σχιζομένους τοὺς οὐρανοὺς καὶ τὸ πνεῦμα ὡς περιστερὰν καταβαῖνον εἰς αὐτόν·

records.literal_gloss: And immediately going up out of the water he saw being torn open the heavens and the Spirit as a dove coming down into him.

en.L: And immediately, coming up out of the water, {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} saw the heavens being torn open and the Spirit like a dove coming down to {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}.
en.B: The moment {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} came up out of the water, {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} saw the heavens torn apart and the Spirit coming down on {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} like a dove.
en.R: Right away, as Jesus was coming up out of the water, {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} saw heaven torn open. And {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} saw the Spirit coming down on {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} like a dove.

vi.L: Và lập tức, khi đang lên khỏi nước, {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} thấy các tầng trời bị xé ra và Thánh Linh như chim bồ câu giáng xuống trên {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}}.
vi.B: Vừa lên khỏi nước, {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} liền thấy các tầng trời xé toạc ra và Thánh Linh giáng xuống trên {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} như chim bồ câu.
vi.R: Ngay lúc Đức Giê-xu từ dưới nước đi lên, {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} thấy bầu trời bị xé ra. Ngài cũng thấy Thánh Linh đang xuống trên {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} như một con chim bồ câu.

ko.L: 그리고 곧 물에서 올라오시면서, 그분은 하늘이 찢어지는 것과 성령께서 비둘기처럼 자신에게로 내려오시는 것을 보셨다.
ko.B: 예수께서 물에서 올라오시자마자, 하늘이 찢어져 열리고 성령께서 비둘기처럼 자신에게 내려오시는 것을 보셨다.
ko.R: 예수께서 물에서 올라오실 때, 곧바로 하늘이 찢어지듯 열리는 것을 보셨다. 그리고 성령께서 비둘기처럼 그분 위로 내려오시는 것도 보셨다.

es.L: Y enseguida, subiendo del agua, vio los cielos rasgándose y al Espíritu, como paloma, descendiendo hacia {{deity_pronoun:él|Él}}.
es.B: En cuanto salió del agua, vio que los cielos se rasgaban y que el Espíritu bajaba sobre {{deity_pronoun:él|Él}} como una paloma.
es.R: Enseguida, cuando Jesús salía del agua, vio que el cielo se rasgaba. Y vio al Espíritu, que bajaba sobre {{deity_pronoun:él|Él}} como una paloma.

fr.L: Et aussitôt, remontant de l’eau, {{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} vit les cieux qui se déchiraient et l’Esprit qui, comme une colombe, descendait sur {{deity_pronoun:lui|Lui}}.
fr.B: Au moment où {{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} remontait de l’eau, {{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} vit les cieux se déchirer et l’Esprit descendre sur {{deity_pronoun:lui|Lui}} comme une colombe.
fr.R: Tout de suite, pendant que Jésus sortait de l’eau, {{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} a vu le ciel se déchirer. Et {{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} a vu l’Esprit descendre sur {{deity_pronoun:lui|Lui}} comme une colombe.

decisions.choice: immediately: Mark's word for moving the story straight on
decisions.reason: Mark uses this word more than forty times, eleven in this chapter. Often it means "at once"; sometimes it just carries the reader into the next event.

decisions.choice: torn open: a violent tearing, not a gentle opening
decisions.reason: The same verb is used when the temple curtain is torn from top to bottom at Jesus' death (15:38). Isaiah 64:1 asks God to tear open the heavens and come down.

decisions.choice: he saw: Jesus is the one who sees
decisions.reason: The subject is still Jesus, who is coming up out of the water, and the voice in 1:11 speaks to him.

decisions.choice: like a dove: the Spirit's coming down is compared to a dove
alternatives: the Spirit took the bodily form of a dove
decisions.reason: The words can describe the way the Spirit came down or what was seen. Luke 3:22 says it was in bodily form; Mark only gives the comparison.

decisions.choice: to him: the Spirit came down upon him
decisions.reason: The word can mean "into", but after a verb of coming down it is often "to" or "upon", as in Matthew 3:16.

decisions.choice: immediately (L); the moment (B); right away (R)
decisions.reason: Literal keeps one word for this Greek word throughout. Balanced and Readable vary it, so that Mark's quick pace does not become a repeated word in English.

decisions.choice: "lập tức" (L); "liền", "vừa ... liền", "ngay" (B); "ngay lúc", "ngay sau đó" (R) for Mark's "immediately"
decisions.reason: Mark uses the word very often to move the story on. Literal keeps one word so the reader sees it recur; Balanced and Readable use the shorter words Vietnamese uses for the same quickness. Holds for the book.

decisions.choice: "곧" (L) for Mark's "immediately" throughout; "-자마자", "곧바로", "바로", "즉시" as the sentence allows (B, R)
decisions.reason: Mark uses the word over forty times to move the story on (meaning decision). Literal keeps one Korean word for it, so the reader can see the repetition; Balanced and Readable vary it as natural Korean does.

decisions.choice: "성령께서 ... 내려오시는" with the honorific
decisions.reason: The Spirit is God and takes "께서" and -시- in the narrative, as in John 1:32. Here "the Spirit" alone is the Holy Spirit, so Korean says "성령" (style guide).

decisions.choice: enseguida (L, R); en cuanto, al instante, en ese momento (B)
decisions.reason: Mark's word for moving the story straight on (meaning decision m1). Literal says "enseguida" every time so readers can see how often Mark uses it; Balanced uses whatever Spanish says most naturally in the sentence; Readable keeps "enseguida". This applies throughout the book.

decisions.choice: rasgarse
decisions.reason: A tearing apart, not a gentle opening (meaning decision m2); Spanish "abrirse" would lose the force, and "rasgar" is the verb used for the temple curtain in 15:38.

decisions.choice: aussitôt (L); varied at Balanced ("au moment où", "aussitôt", "sans tarder", "sur-le-champ"); tout de suite (R), for the whole book
decisions.reason: Mark's favourite connective (meaning decision m1). Literal keeps one word, "aussitôt", so the reader can see how often Mark uses it; Balanced lets the French sentence decide, as the English does; Readable says "tout de suite", the everyday word.

source.text: καὶ φωνὴ ἐγένετο ἐκ τῶν οὐρανῶν· Σὺ εἶ ὁ υἱός μου ὁ ἀγαπητός, ἐν σοὶ εὐδόκησα.

records.literal_gloss: And a voice came out of the heavens, You are the Son of me the beloved, in you I was well pleased.

en.L: And a voice came out of the heavens: "You are {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} Son, the beloved; in {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} I am well pleased."
en.B: Then a voice spoke from heaven: "You are {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} dearly loved Son. I take delight in {{deity_pronoun:you|You}}."
en.R: Then a voice from heaven said, "You are {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} Son, and I love {{deity_pronoun:you|You}}. I am very pleased with {{deity_pronoun:you|You}}."

vi.L: Và có tiếng từ các tầng trời: "Con là Con của {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}}, Đấng yêu dấu; {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}} đẹp lòng về Con."
vi.B: Rồi có tiếng từ trời phán: "Con là Con yêu dấu của {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}}. Ta rất vui lòng về Con."
vi.R: Rồi có tiếng từ trời phán: "Con là Con của {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}}, và {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}} yêu thương Con. Ta rất hài lòng về Con."

ko.L: 그리고 하늘들에서 소리가 났다. "너는 나의 아들, 사랑하는 [아들]이다. 너를 내가 기뻐한다."
ko.B: 그때 하늘에서 소리가 들려왔다. "너는 내가 사랑하는 아들이다. 나는 너를 기뻐한다."
ko.R: 그러자 하늘에서 소리가 들렸다. "너는 내 아들이다. 나는 너를 사랑한다. 나는 너를 무척 기뻐한다."

es.L: Y vino una voz de los cielos: «Tú eres {{deity_pronoun:mi|Mi}} Hijo, el amado; en {{deity_pronoun:ti|Ti}} me he complacido».
es.B: Entonces una voz habló desde el cielo: «Tú eres {{deity_pronoun:mi|Mi}} Hijo amado; en {{deity_pronoun:ti|Ti}} me complazco».
es.R: Entonces una voz del cielo dijo: «Tú eres {{deity_pronoun:mi|Mi}} Hijo, y {{deity_pronoun:te|Te}} amo. En {{deity_pronoun:ti|Ti}} encuentro {{deity_pronoun:mi|Mi}} alegría».

fr.L: Et une voix vint des cieux : « Tu es {{deity_pronoun:mon|Mon}} Fils, le bien-aimé ; en {{deity_pronoun:toi|Toi}} je prends plaisir. »
fr.B: Puis une voix se fit entendre du ciel : « Tu es {{deity_pronoun:mon|Mon}} Fils bien-aimé ; en {{deity_pronoun:toi|Toi}} je trouve toute {{deity_pronoun:ma|Ma}} joie. »
fr.R: Puis une voix venant du ciel a dit : « Tu es {{deity_pronoun:mon|Mon}} Fils, et je {{deity_pronoun:t’|T’}}aime. Je suis très content de {{deity_pronoun:toi|Toi}}. »

decisions.choice: you are my Son ... I am well pleased: Psalm 2:7 and Isaiah 42:1
decisions.reason: In Psalm 2:7 God says to his anointed king, "You are my son". In Isaiah 42:1 God delights in his chosen servant and puts his Spirit on him. "Beloved son" also recalls Isaac (Genesis 22:2).

decisions.choice: I am well pleased: a settled delight
alternatives: God became pleased at the baptism
decisions.reason: The past tense here states God's approval as a fact, not a change that has just happened.

decisions.choice: You are: the voice speaks to Jesus himself
alternatives: the voice speaks about him to the crowd
decisions.reason: In Mark the voice says "you". Matthew 3:17 has "This is", addressed to those present.

decisions.choice: Son with a capital letter
decisions.reason: The word is a title here, as in 1:1 and 15:39, so it is capitalized, as at Matthew 3:17.

decisions.choice: the voice says "Ta" and "Con" for "you"; "phán" (B, R)
decisions.reason: The Father speaks to the Son as a father does, "Con", a noun of address that is always capitalised and takes no setting span (style guide, section 7). "phán" is kept for God speaking.

decisions.choice: "하늘들" (L), "하늘" (B, R); "사랑하는 [아들]" (L)
decisions.reason: Literal keeps the Greek plural "heavens", which Korean can mark with "-들"; Balanced and Readable use the ordinary singular. The Greek adds "the beloved" after "my Son" as a second title; Literal keeps it apart and brackets the noun Korean needs. The Father speaks to the Son in the plain style (해라체), as in 1:2.

decisions.choice: «Tú eres» plain; no span on the reflexive "me"
decisions.reason: "Tú" opens the quoted sentence, so it is capitalised either way and written plain. In "me complazco" the pronoun only marks the verb as reflexive, as in Hebrews 3:11, and stands for no English word, so it takes no setting.

decisions.choice: en toi je prends plaisir (L); en toi je trouve toute ma joie (B); je suis très content de toi (R)
alternatives: en toi j’ai mis toute mon affection
decisions.reason: The verb speaks of a settled delight (meaning decision m2). The familiar older wording speaks of affection, which is not the sense; Balanced says "joie", and its "ma", God speaking, takes a deity_pronoun span like "mon".

source.text: Καὶ εὐθὺς τὸ πνεῦμα αὐτὸν ἐκβάλλει εἰς τὴν ἔρημον.

records.literal_gloss: And immediately the Spirit him drives out into the wilderness.

en.L: And immediately the Spirit drives {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} out into the wilderness.
en.B: Straight away the Spirit drove {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} out into the wilderness.
en.R: Right after that, the Spirit pushed Jesus to go out into the desert.

vi.L: Và lập tức Thánh Linh đẩy {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} ra đồng hoang.
vi.B: Ngay sau đó, Thánh Linh đẩy {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} vào đồng hoang.
vi.R: Ngay sau đó, Thánh Linh thúc Đức Giê-xu đi vào sa mạc.

ko.L: 그리고 곧 성령께서 그분을 광야로 내모신다.
ko.B: 곧이어 성령께서 예수를 광야로 내모셨다.
ko.R: 그 뒤 바로 성령께서 예수를 빈 들로 떠밀어 보내셨다.

es.L: Y enseguida el Espíritu {{deity_pronoun:lo|Lo}} echa fuera, al desierto.
es.B: Enseguida el Espíritu {{deity_pronoun:lo|Lo}} impulsó a salir al desierto.
es.R: Enseguida, el Espíritu hizo que Jesús se fuera al desierto.

fr.L: Et aussitôt l’Esprit {{deity_pronoun:le|Le}} pousse au désert.
fr.B: Aussitôt après, l’Esprit {{deity_pronoun:le|Le}} poussa au désert.
fr.R: Tout de suite après, l’Esprit a poussé Jésus à aller dans le désert.

decisions.choice: drives out: sends with force
decisions.reason: This is the verb used for casting out demons (1:34, 39). It shows urgency and the Spirit's power, not hostility. Matthew 4:1 and Luke 4:1 say "led".

decisions.choice: drives: the present tense of storytelling
decisions.reason: Mark often tells past events in the present tense to make them vivid.

decisions.choice: the wilderness: where Israel was tested
decisions.reason: Israel was led through the wilderness for forty years and tested there (Deuteronomy 8:2).

decisions.choice: drives (L); drove (B); pushed ... to go (R)
decisions.reason: Literal keeps Mark's present tense. Balanced and Readable use the past, as English tells a story.

decisions.choice: historic present kept at Literal by leaving out "đã" ("đẩy", 1:21 "vào", 1:30 "nói")
decisions.reason: Vietnamese has no verb endings; Literal keeps Mark's present-tense storytelling by not adding "đã", as the style guide says, while Balanced and Readable tell it as plain narrative. Holds for the chapter.

decisions.choice: historic present at Literal ("내모신다", "들어간다", "말씀하신다"); past at Balanced and Readable, through Mark 1
decisions.reason: Mark often tells past events in the present for vividness (meaning decision); Korean narrative can do the same, so Literal keeps it, as the Korean of John does. One decision for the chapter.

decisions.choice: present tense (L); past tense (B, R)
decisions.reason: As in John: Mark often tells his story in the present tense (meaning decision m2). Literal keeps it; Balanced and Readable use the past, as Spanish stories do. This applies throughout the book.

decisions.choice: pousse (L); poussa (B)
decisions.reason: The verb means to send out with force (meaning decision m1). "Pousser" keeps the force without the hostility of "chasser", the French word used for driving out demons.

source.text: καὶ ἦν ἐν τῇ ἐρήμῳ τεσσεράκοντα ἡμέρας πειραζόμενος ὑπὸ τοῦ Σατανᾶ, καὶ ἦν μετὰ τῶν θηρίων, καὶ οἱ ἄγγελοι διηκόνουν αὐτῷ.

records.literal_gloss: And he was in the wilderness forty days being tempted by the Satan, and was with the wild beasts, and the angels were serving him.

en.L: And {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} was in the wilderness forty days, being tempted by Satan, and {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} was with the wild animals, and the angels were serving {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}.
en.B: He stayed in the wilderness for forty days while Satan tempted {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}. He was among the wild animals, and the angels took care of {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}.
en.R: Jesus was in the desert for forty days, and Satan tried to make {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} do wrong. Wild animals were there with {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}, and angels took care of {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}.

vi.L: Và {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} ở trong đồng hoang bốn mươi ngày, bị Sa-tan cám dỗ, và {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} ở với các thú dữ, và các thiên sứ phục vụ {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}}.
vi.B: Ngài ở trong đồng hoang bốn mươi ngày, chịu Sa-tan cám dỗ. Ngài ở giữa các thú dữ, và các thiên sứ chăm sóc {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}}.
vi.R: Đức Giê-xu ở trong sa mạc bốn mươi ngày, và Sa-tan tìm cách khiến {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} làm điều sai. Có thú dữ ở đó với {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}}, và các thiên sứ chăm sóc {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}}.

ko.L: 그리고 그분은 사십 일 동안 광야에 계시면서 사탄에게 시험을 받으셨다. 그리고 들짐승들과 함께 계셨고, 천사들이 그분을 섬기고 있었다.
ko.B: 예수께서는 사십 일 동안 광야에 계시면서 사탄에게 시험을 받으셨다. 들짐승들과 함께 지내셨고, 천사들이 그분의 시중을 들었다.
ko.R: 예수께서는 빈 들에서 사십 일을 지내셨다. 그동안 사탄이 예수를 꾀어 죄를 짓게 하려고 했다. 들짐승들도 그곳에 함께 있었고, 천사들이 예수를 돌보아 드렸다.

es.L: Y estuvo en el desierto cuarenta días, siendo tentado por Satanás, y estaba con las fieras, y los ángeles {{deity_pronoun:le|Le}} servían.
es.B: Permaneció en el desierto cuarenta días mientras Satanás {{deity_pronoun:lo|Lo}} tentaba. Estaba entre los animales salvajes, y los ángeles {{deity_pronoun:lo|Lo}} atendían.
es.R: Jesús estuvo en el desierto cuarenta días, y Satanás {{deity_pronoun:lo|Lo}} ponía a prueba para que hiciera lo malo. Los animales salvajes estaban allí con {{deity_pronoun:él|Él}}, y los ángeles {{deity_pronoun:lo|Lo}} cuidaban.

fr.L: Et {{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} était dans le désert quarante jours, tenté par Satan ; et {{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} était avec les bêtes sauvages, et les anges {{deity_pronoun:le|Le}} servaient.
fr.B: Il resta quarante jours dans le désert, où Satan {{deity_pronoun:le|Le}} tentait. Il vivait parmi les bêtes sauvages, et les anges prenaient soin de {{deity_pronoun:lui|Lui}}.
fr.R: Jésus est resté quarante jours dans le désert, et Satan a essayé de {{deity_pronoun:le|Le}} pousser à faire le mal. Des bêtes sauvages étaient là avec {{deity_pronoun:lui|Lui}}, et des anges prenaient soin de {{deity_pronoun:lui|Lui}}.

decisions.choice: tempted: put to the test, here by one who wants him to fail
alternatives: only tested to show his strength
decisions.reason: The word covers both testing and temptation. Satan's aim is to make Jesus turn from God's way.

decisions.choice: Satan: the adversary, the enemy of God
decisions.reason: The name means accuser or adversary. Matthew and Luke call him the devil in this story.

decisions.choice: forty days: Israel's forty years, and the forty days of Moses and Elijah
decisions.reason: Israel was tested for forty years in the wilderness. Moses was on the mountain forty days (Exodus 34:28), and Elijah walked forty days to Horeb (1 Kings 19:8).

decisions.choice: with the wild animals: in dangerous, empty country
alternatives: at peace with the animals, as in Isaiah 11:6-9
decisions.reason: Mark does not say what the animals mean. They show how wild the place was; some read them as a sign of the peace of God's new age.

decisions.choice: were serving him: caring for his needs
decisions.reason: The same verb is used of Simon's mother-in-law in 1:31. Angels brought Elijah food in the wilderness (1 Kings 19:5-7).

decisions.choice: tried to make him do wrong
decisions.reason: Readable says what tempting means in plain words, as in Matthew 4:1.

decisions.choice: "시험을 받으셨다" (L, B)
decisions.reason: "시험" covers both testing and tempting, as the Greek word does (meaning decision); "유혹" names only the enticement. Readable says what Satan tried to do, as the English Readable does.

source.text: Καὶ μετὰ τὸ παραδοθῆναι τὸν Ἰωάννην ἦλθεν ὁ Ἰησοῦς εἰς τὴν Γαλιλαίαν κηρύσσων τὸ εὐαγγέλιον τοῦ θεοῦ καὶ λέγων ὅτι Πεπλήρωται ὁ καιρὸς καὶ ἤγγικεν ἡ βασιλεία τοῦ θεοῦ· μετανοεῖτε καὶ πιστεύετε ἐν τῷ εὐαγγελίῳ.

records.literal_gloss: And after the to be handed over the John came the Jesus into the Galilee proclaiming the gospel of the God \v 15 and saying, Has been fulfilled the time and has come near the kingdom of the God; repent and believe in the gospel.

en.L: And after John was handed over, Jesus came into Galilee, proclaiming the gospel of God \v 15 and saying, "The time has been fulfilled, and the kingdom of God has come near; repent and believe in the gospel."
en.B: After John had been handed over, Jesus went into Galilee, proclaiming God's gospel. \v 15 "The appointed time has arrived in full," {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} said, "and the kingdom of God has come near. Repent, and believe in the gospel."
en.R: After John was put in prison, Jesus went to Galilee and told people the good news from God. \v 15 He said, "The time God promised has come. The kingdom of God is coming near. Turn away from your sins and come back to God, and believe the good news!"

vi.L: Và sau khi Giăng bị nộp, Đức Giê-xu đến Ga-li-lê, rao giảng Tin Lành của Đức Chúa Trời \v 15 và nói rằng: "Thời kỳ đã được trọn, và vương quốc của Đức Chúa Trời đã đến gần; hãy ăn năn và tin vào Tin Lành."
vi.B: Sau khi Giăng bị bắt nộp, Đức Giê-xu đi đến Ga-li-lê, rao giảng Tin Lành của Đức Chúa Trời. \v 15 Ngài nói: "Thời kỳ đã định nay đã đến trọn, và vương quốc của Đức Chúa Trời đã đến gần. Hãy ăn năn và tin vào Tin Lành."
vi.R: Sau khi Giăng bị bỏ tù, Đức Giê-xu đi đến miền Ga-li-lê và nói cho người ta biết Tin Lành từ Đức Chúa Trời. \v 15 Ngài nói: "Thời điểm Đức Chúa Trời đã hứa nay đã đến. Vương quốc của Đức Chúa Trời đang đến gần. Hãy từ bỏ tội lỗi, quay về với Đức Chúa Trời, và hãy tin nhận Tin Lành!"

ko.L: 그리고 요한이 넘겨진 뒤에 예수께서 갈릴리로 오셔서 하나님의 복음을 선포하시며 \v 15 말씀하셨다. "그 때가 채워졌고 하나님의 나라가 가까이 다가왔다. 회개하여라. 그리고 복음을 믿어라."
ko.B: 요한이 잡혀 넘겨진 뒤에 예수께서 갈릴리로 가셔서 하나님의 복음을 선포하셨다. \v 15 예수께서 말씀하셨다. "하나님께서 정하신 때가 이제 다 찼다. 하나님의 나라가 가까이 와 있다. 회개하고 복음을 믿어라."
ko.R: 요한이 감옥에 갇힌 뒤에 예수께서 갈릴리로 가셔서, 하나님께서 주신 기쁜 소식을 사람들에게 전하셨다. \v 15 예수께서 말씀하셨다. "하나님께서 약속하신 때가 왔다. 하나님의 나라가 가까이 오고 있다. 죄에서 돌이켜 하나님께 돌아오너라. 그리고 이 기쁜 소식을 믿어라!"

es.L: Y después de que Juan fue entregado, vino Jesús a Galilea proclamando el evangelio de Dios \v 15 y diciendo: «El tiempo se ha cumplido, y el reino de Dios se ha acercado; {{plural_you:arrepiéntanse|arrepentíos}} y {{plural_you:crean|creed}} en el evangelio».
es.B: Después de que Juan fue entregado, Jesús fue a Galilea a proclamar el evangelio de Dios. \v 15 «Ha llegado el tiempo señalado —decía—, y el reino de Dios se ha acercado. {{plural_you:Arrepiéntanse|Arrepentíos}} y {{plural_you:crean|creed}} en el evangelio».
es.R: Después de que metieron a Juan en la cárcel, Jesús fue a Galilea y anunciaba la buena noticia que viene de Dios. \v 15 Decía: «Ha llegado el tiempo que Dios prometió. El reino de Dios está cerca. {{plural_you:Apártense|Apartaos}} de {{plural_you:sus|vuestros}} pecados y {{plural_you:vuelvan|volved}} a Dios, y {{plural_you:crean|creed}} la buena noticia».

fr.L: Et après que Jean eut été livré, Jésus vint en Galilée, proclamant l’Évangile de Dieu \v 15 et disant : « Le temps est accompli, et le royaume de Dieu s’est approché ; repentez-vous et croyez en l’Évangile. »
fr.B: Après que Jean eut été livré, Jésus alla en Galilée, où {{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} proclamait l’Évangile de Dieu. \v 15 « Le temps fixé est pleinement arrivé, disait-{{deity_pronoun:il|Il}}, et le royaume de Dieu est tout proche. Repentez-vous, et croyez à l’Évangile. »
fr.R: Après que Jean a été mis en prison, Jésus est allé en Galilée. Il annonçait aux gens la bonne nouvelle qui vient de Dieu. \v 15 Il disait : « Le moment que Dieu avait promis est arrivé. Le royaume de Dieu est tout proche. Détournez-vous de vos péchés et revenez à Dieu, et croyez à la bonne nouvelle ! »

decisions.choice: handed over: arrested and put in prison
decisions.reason: Mark tells of John's arrest in 6:17. The same verb is used of Jesus being handed over (9:31; 14:41) and then of his followers (13:9), so John's path foreshadows theirs.

decisions.choice: the gospel of God: the good news that comes from God
decisions.reason: God is the source of the news. Its content is what Jesus says next: God's kingdom has come near.

decisions.choice: the time has been fulfilled: the time God set has fully come
alternatives: time in general has run out
decisions.reason: The word for time is the appointed moment. What the prophets waited for has arrived.

decisions.choice: has come near: it is close at hand, already pressing in
decisions.reason: The perfect tense says the kingdom has drawn near and is now close. Matthew 4:17 has the same verb. God's rule is breaking in through Jesus' words and works.

decisions.choice: believe in the gospel: trust the message and rely on it
decisions.reason: Believing "in" a message is an unusual phrase. It means putting one's trust in the news that God's kingdom has come near.

decisions.choice: was put in prison
decisions.reason: Readable says what being handed over meant for John, which Mark tells in 6:17.

decisions.choice: turn away from your sins and come back to God
decisions.reason: Readable says what repenting means, as in Matthew 3:2 and 4:17.

decisions.choice: "vương quốc của Đức Chúa Trời" for the kingdom of God
decisions.reason: As in John 3:3-5: "nước" is the traditional word but today reads first as "country"; "vương quốc" keeps the idea of God's rule as king. Used through Mark.

decisions.choice: "하나님의 나라" at every level, through Mark
decisions.reason: As John 3:3 in Korean. "나라" covers both God's reign and the realm where it holds; "천국" (heaven) would suggest a place after death, which is not what Jesus announces here.

decisions.choice: Jesus speaks in 해라체 ("믿어라", "오너라"), through Mark
decisions.reason: The style guide fixes this for the Gospels: Jesus speaks plainly to crowds, disciples and opponents, and people speak to him in 합쇼체, so relationships do not shift between scenes.

decisions.choice: el reino de Dios
decisions.reason: As in John 3:3 and Galatians 5:21, with a lower-case "reino". The same words at every level and throughout Mark.

decisions.choice: fue entregado
decisions.reason: Literal keeps the verb "hand over", which Mark uses again of Jesus (9:31; 14:41; 15:1); meaning decision m1 says it means arrest, which Readable spells out.

decisions.choice: repentez-vous (L, B)
decisions.reason: "Se repentir" is the French word for the turning the Greek verb describes, and it matches "repentance" in 1:4. "Se convertir" now suggests changing religion. Readable says what it means, as the English Readable does.

decisions.choice: croyez en (L); croyez à (B, R)
decisions.reason: Literal follows the Greek preposition. "Croire à" is the ordinary French for trusting that a message is true (meaning decision m5).

source.text: Καὶ παράγων παρὰ τὴν θάλασσαν τῆς Γαλιλαίας εἶδεν Σίμωνα καὶ Ἀνδρέαν τὸν ἀδελφὸν Σίμωνος ἀμφιβάλλοντας ἐν τῇ θαλάσσῃ, ἦσαν γὰρ ἁλιεῖς·

records.literal_gloss: And passing by beside the sea of the Galilee he saw Simon and Andrew the brother of Simon casting in the sea; they were for fishermen.

en.L: And passing along beside the Sea of Galilee, {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} saw Simon and Andrew, Simon's brother, casting [a net] in the sea, for they were fishermen.
en.B: As Jesus went along the shore of the Sea of Galilee, {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} saw Simon and Simon's brother Andrew throwing a net into the water. They fished for a living.
en.R: One day Jesus was walking beside Lake Galilee. He saw Simon and his brother Andrew throwing a net into the lake to catch fish, because they were fishermen.

vi.L: Và đang đi dọc theo biển Ga-li-lê, {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} thấy Si-môn và Anh-rê, người anh em của Si-môn, đang quăng [lưới] xuống biển, vì họ là những người đánh cá.
vi.B: Khi đi dọc theo bờ biển Ga-li-lê, {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} thấy Si-môn và Anh-rê, người anh em của Si-môn, đang quăng lưới xuống nước. Họ làm nghề đánh cá.
vi.R: Một hôm, Đức Giê-xu đang đi dọc bờ biển hồ Ga-li-lê. Ngài thấy Si-môn và Anh-rê, anh em ruột của ông, đang quăng lưới xuống hồ để bắt cá, vì họ là dân đánh cá.

ko.L: 그리고 갈릴리 바다 곁을 지나가시다가, 그분은 시몬과 시몬의 형제 안드레가 바다에 [그물을] 던지고 있는 것을 보셨다. 그들은 어부였기 때문이다.
ko.B: 예수께서 갈릴리 바닷가를 따라 걸어가시다가, 시몬과 그의 형제 안드레가 바다에 그물을 던지는 것을 보셨다. 그들은 고기잡이로 살아가는 어부였다.
ko.R: 어느 날 예수께서 갈릴리 호숫가를 걷고 계셨다. 그때 시몬과 그의 형제 안드레가 호수에 그물을 던져 고기를 잡고 있는 것을 보셨다. 그들은 어부였다.

es.L: Y pasando junto al mar de Galilea, vio a Simón y a Andrés, el hermano de Simón, echando [la red] en el mar, porque eran pescadores.
es.B: Mientras Jesús caminaba por la orilla del mar de Galilea, vio a Simón y a Andrés, hermano de Simón, echando la red al agua. Se ganaban la vida pescando.
es.R: Un día Jesús caminaba junto al lago de Galilea. Vio a Simón y a su hermano Andrés, que echaban una red al lago para pescar, porque eran pescadores.

fr.L: Et passant le long de la mer de Galilée, {{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} vit Simon et André, le frère de Simon, jetant [le filet] dans la mer, car ils étaient pêcheurs.
fr.B: Comme Jésus longeait la mer de Galilée, {{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} vit Simon et André, le frère de Simon, qui jetaient un filet dans l’eau. C’étaient des pêcheurs de métier.
fr.R: Un jour, Jésus marchait au bord du lac de Galilée. Il a vu Simon et son frère André, qui jetaient un filet dans le lac pour attraper des poissons. C’étaient des pêcheurs.

decisions.choice: the Sea of Galilee: a freshwater lake about thirteen miles long
decisions.reason: The Greek calls it a sea, following Hebrew usage, but it is a large lake. Fishing was one of the main trades of the towns on its shore.

decisions.choice: casting: throwing a round net by hand
decisions.reason: The verb itself means throwing around; it was used for a casting net, thrown from the shore or from shallow water.

decisions.choice: a net (L in brackets, B, R); Jesus (B, R)
decisions.reason: English needs an object for "casting". Balanced and Readable name Jesus, since the last sentence spoke of him only by "he".

decisions.choice: Lake Galilee
decisions.reason: Readable calls it a lake, which is what it is, as in Matthew 4:18.

decisions.choice: "biển" (L, B); "biển hồ" here, then "hồ" (R)
decisions.reason: As in John 6:1: the Sea of Galilee is a freshwater lake. Literal and Balanced keep "biển", the name readers know; Readable says "biển hồ" once and "hồ" after it.

decisions.choice: "người anh em" (brother), not "anh" or "em"
decisions.reason: Vietnamese usually says whether a brother is older or younger; Mark does not, so the open word is kept, as in John 1:40.

decisions.choice: "갈릴리 바다" (L, B); "갈릴리 호수" (R)
decisions.reason: As John 6:1 in Korean: "갈릴리 바다" is the established name and keeps Mark's word "sea"; Readable says "호수" (lake), as the English Readable does, since it is a freshwater lake (meaning decision).

decisions.choice: "형제"
decisions.reason: Korean usually says whether a brother is older or younger, but Mark does not say which of the two was older, so the neutral "형제" is kept, as in John 1:40.

decisions.choice: mar de Galilea (L, B); lago de Galilea (R)
decisions.reason: "Mar de Galilea" is the name Spanish readers know, as in John 6:1; Readable says plainly that it is a lake (meaning decision m1).

source.text: καὶ εἶπεν αὐτοῖς ὁ Ἰησοῦς· Δεῦτε ὀπίσω μου, καὶ ποιήσω ὑμᾶς γενέσθαι ἁλιεῖς ἀνθρώπων.

records.literal_gloss: And said to them the Jesus, Come after me, and I will make you to become fishers of men.

en.L: And Jesus said to them, "Come after {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}}, and I will make you become fishers of {{gender:people|men}}."
en.B: Jesus said to them, "Come and follow {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}}. I will make you into fishers of {{gender:people|men}}."
en.R: Jesus said to them, "Come, follow {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}}. I will teach you to catch {{gender:people|men}} instead of fish."

vi.L: Và Đức Giê-xu nói với họ: "Hãy đến theo sau {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}}, và {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}} sẽ làm cho các anh trở thành những người đánh lưới người."
vi.B: Đức Giê-xu nói với họ: "Hãy đến và theo {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}}. Ta sẽ làm cho các anh thành những người đánh lưới người."
vi.R: Đức Giê-xu nói với họ: "Hãy đến, đi theo {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}}. Ta sẽ dạy các anh đi tìm người cho Đức Chúa Trời, thay vì đi bắt cá."

ko.L: 예수께서 그들에게 말씀하셨다. "내 뒤에 오너라. 그러면 너희가 사람들을 낚는 어부가 되도록 내가 만들겠다."
ko.B: 예수께서 그들에게 말씀하셨다. "와서 나를 따라라. 내가 너희를 사람들을 낚는 어부로 삼겠다."
ko.R: 예수께서 그들에게 말씀하셨다. "와서 나를 따라오너라. 이제 너희는 물고기 대신 사람들을 모으게 될 것이다. 내가 그렇게 해 주겠다."

es.L: Y les dijo Jesús: «{{plural_you:Vengan|Venid}} detrás de {{deity_pronoun:mí|Mí}}, y haré que {{plural_you:lleguen|lleguéis}} a ser pescadores de {{gender:personas|hombres}}».
es.B: Jesús les dijo: «{{plural_you:Vengan y síganme|Venid y seguidme}}. Yo {{plural_you:los|os}} haré pescadores de {{gender:personas|hombres}}».
es.R: Jesús les dijo: «{{plural_you:Vengan, síganme|Venid, seguidme}}. Yo {{plural_you:les|os}} enseñaré a pescar {{gender:personas|hombres}} en vez de peces».

fr.L: Et Jésus leur dit : « Venez derrière {{deity_pronoun:moi|Moi}}, et je vous ferai devenir pêcheurs {{gender:d’êtres humains|d’hommes}}. »
fr.B: Jésus leur dit : « Venez, suivez-{{deity_pronoun:moi|Moi}}, et je ferai de vous des pêcheurs {{gender:d’êtres humains|d’hommes}}. »
fr.R: Jésus leur a dit : « Venez avec {{deity_pronoun:moi|Moi}} ! Je vais vous apprendre à pêcher des {{gender:gens|hommes}} au lieu de poissons. »

decisions.choice: come after me: become my disciples, following me as your teacher
alternatives: walk behind me for a while
decisions.reason: Disciples walked behind their teacher, learning from him as they went.

decisions.choice: fishers of people: they will gather people for God's kingdom
alternatives: a threat of judgment, as fishing is in Jeremiah 16:16
decisions.reason: Jesus takes their trade as a picture of their new work, bringing people in to God's kingdom.

decisions.choice: men: human beings
decisions.reason: The word is the general word for human beings, so the gender setting applies.

decisions.choice: I will make you become: they will grow into this work
alternatives: they are fishers of people at once
decisions.reason: Mark has "become", which Matthew 4:19 does not. The change takes time, and the disciples are sent out in 6:7.

decisions.choice: Jesus calls the fishermen "các anh"
decisions.reason: The style guide has Jesus call his disciples "các con"; at their call these men are not yet his disciples, so he speaks to them as adults, as in John 1:38-51.

decisions.choice: no gender span on "người" (people)
decisions.reason: "người" already means men and women alike; the English traditional alternative "men" has no Vietnamese counterpart that would mean the same.

decisions.choice: "đi tìm người cho Đức Chúa Trời, thay vì đi bắt cá" (R)
decisions.reason: "bắt người" would mean "arrest people". Readable says what the picture means, gathering people for God, as the meaning decision explains it.

decisions.choice: "사람들" with no gender span
decisions.reason: The English needs a gender span for "people|men"; the Korean "사람" already means human beings of either sex and has no traditional masculine counterpart in this phrase, so there is nothing for the setting to change (style guide, section 7).

decisions.choice: "사람들을 모으게 될 것이다" (R) for "fishers of people"
decisions.reason: Literal and Balanced keep the picture "사람들을 낚는 어부". In everyday Korean "낚다" also means to trick someone, which a new reader could hear; Readable keeps the contrast with fish and says what the picture means, gathering people (meaning decision).

decisions.choice: síganme / seguidme, no deity_pronoun span
decisions.reason: The pronoun for Jesus is joined to the end of the verb, so it cannot take the capital (see 1:2). Literal keeps "detrás de mí", where the free pronoun takes the setting.

decisions.choice: {{gender:personas|hombres}}
decisions.reason: The Greek word means human beings (meaning decision m3); the reader setting gives the traditional "hombres".

decisions.choice: pêcheurs {{gender:d’êtres humains|d’hommes}} (L, B); des {{gender:gens|hommes}} (R)
decisions.reason: The word means human beings (meaning decision m3), so the inclusive wording is the default and the familiar "pêcheurs d’hommes" the alternative, as in English.

source.text: καὶ εὐθὺς ἀφέντες τὰ δίκτυα ἠκολούθησαν αὐτῷ.

records.literal_gloss: And immediately having left the nets they followed him.

en.L: And immediately, leaving the nets, they followed {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}.
en.B: They dropped their nets on the spot and followed {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}.
en.R: Right away they left their nets and followed {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}.

vi.L: Và lập tức, bỏ lưới lại, họ đi theo {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}}.
vi.B: Họ liền bỏ lưới lại mà đi theo {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}}.
vi.R: Ngay lập tức, họ bỏ lưới lại và đi theo {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}}.

ko.L: 그리고 곧 그들은 그물을 버려두고 그분을 따라갔다.
ko.B: 그들은 그 자리에서 그물을 버려두고 예수를 따라갔다.
ko.R: 그들은 바로 그물을 내려놓고 예수를 따라갔다.

es.L: Y enseguida, dejando las redes, {{deity_pronoun:lo|Lo}} siguieron.
es.B: Al instante dejaron sus redes y {{deity_pronoun:lo|Lo}} siguieron.
es.R: Enseguida dejaron sus redes y {{deity_pronoun:lo|Lo}} siguieron.

fr.L: Et aussitôt, laissant les filets, ils {{deity_pronoun:le|Le}} suivirent.
fr.B: Sur-le-champ, ils laissèrent leurs filets et {{deity_pronoun:le|Le}} suivirent.
fr.R: Tout de suite, ils ont laissé leurs filets et ils {{deity_pronoun:l’|L’}}ont suivi.

decisions.choice: followed him: went with him as his disciples
alternatives: walked behind him for a short time
decisions.reason: To follow a teacher was to become his disciple and share his life.

decisions.choice: immediately ... leaving: a response with no delay or conditions
decisions.reason: They leave their nets, their living, at once (see 10:28).

decisions.choice: seguir
decisions.reason: Every level keeps "seguir", which carries both senses: walking after someone and becoming his disciple (meaning decision m1), as in John 1:37.

source.text: καὶ προβὰς ὀλίγον εἶδεν Ἰάκωβον τὸν τοῦ Ζεβεδαίου καὶ Ἰωάννην τὸν ἀδελφὸν αὐτοῦ, καὶ αὐτοὺς ἐν τῷ πλοίῳ καταρτίζοντας τὰ δίκτυα, καὶ εὐθὺς ἐκάλεσεν αὐτούς.

records.literal_gloss: And having gone on a little he saw James the [son] of the Zebedee and John the brother of him, and them in the boat mending the nets, \v 20 and immediately he called them.

en.L: And going on a little, {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} saw James the [son] of Zebedee and John his brother, and they [were] in the boat mending the nets, \v 20 and immediately {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} called them.
en.B: He went on a little way and saw James son of Zebedee and his brother John, who were in their boat putting their nets in order. \v 20 He called them at once.
en.R: Jesus walked on a little farther and saw James and John, the sons of Zebedee. They were in their boat, fixing their fishing nets. \v 20 Right away Jesus called them to come with {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}.

vi.L: Và đi thêm một chút, {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} thấy Gia-cơ [con] của Xê-bê-đê và Giăng, người anh em của ông, và họ đang ở trong thuyền vá lưới, \v 20 và lập tức {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} gọi họ.
vi.B: Đi thêm một quãng ngắn, {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} thấy Gia-cơ con Xê-bê-đê và Giăng, người anh em của ông, đang ở trong thuyền sửa soạn lưới. \v 20 Ngài liền gọi họ.
vi.R: Đức Giê-xu đi thêm một đoạn nữa và thấy Gia-cơ và Giăng, hai con trai của Xê-bê-đê. Họ đang ngồi trong thuyền vá lưới. \v 20 Ngay lúc đó, Đức Giê-xu gọi họ đi theo {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}}.

ko.L: 그리고 조금 더 가시다가 그분은 세베대의 [아들] 야고보와 그의 형제 요한을 보셨는데, 그들도 배에서 그물을 손질하고 있었다. \v 20 그리고 곧 그분이 그들을 부르셨다.
ko.B: 예수께서 조금 더 가시다가 세베대의 아들 야고보와 그의 형제 요한을 보셨다. 그들은 배에서 그물을 정리하고 있었다. \v 20 예수께서 곧바로 그들을 부르셨다.
ko.R: 예수께서 조금 더 걸어가시다가 세베대의 두 아들 야고보와 요한을 보셨다. 그들은 배 안에서 고기잡이 그물을 고치고 있었다. \v 20 예수께서는 바로 그들에게 함께 가자고 부르셨다.

es.L: Y avanzando un poco, vio a Santiago, el [hijo] de Zebedeo, y a Juan, su hermano, y ellos [estaban] en la barca remendando las redes, \v 20 y enseguida los llamó.
es.B: Un poco más adelante vio a Santiago, hijo de Zebedeo, y a su hermano Juan, que estaban en su barca arreglando las redes. \v 20 Enseguida los llamó.
es.R: Jesús caminó un poco más y vio a Santiago y a Juan, los hijos de Zebedeo. Estaban en su barca arreglando sus redes de pescar. \v 20 Enseguida Jesús los llamó para que fueran con {{deity_pronoun:él|Él}}.

fr.L: Et étant allé un peu plus loin, {{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} vit Jacques, le [fils] de Zébédée, et Jean son frère, eux aussi dans la barque, réparant les filets, \v 20 et aussitôt {{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} les appela.
fr.B: Il alla un peu plus loin et vit Jacques, fils de Zébédée, et son frère Jean, qui étaient dans leur barque et remettaient leurs filets en état. \v 20 Aussitôt, {{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} les appela.
