fr.R: Jésus est allé un peu plus loin et a vu Jacques et Jean, les fils de Zébédée. Ils étaient dans leur bateau et ils réparaient leurs filets de pêche. \v 20 Tout de suite, Jésus les a appelés à venir avec {{deity_pronoun:lui|Lui}}.

decisions.choice: mending: repairing or getting the nets ready
decisions.reason: The word means to put in order: to mend what is torn or to make the nets ready for use.

decisions.choice: the [son] of Zebedee: the article stands for "son"
decisions.reason: Greek often names a man by his father with the article alone. Zebedee is their father (1:20).

decisions.choice: called them: summoned them to be his disciples
decisions.reason: Jesus calls them as he called Simon and Andrew (1:17), and they follow (1:20).

decisions.choice: called them to come with him
decisions.reason: Readable says what the call was for, as in Matthew 4:21.

decisions.choice: "Gia-cơ" for James; "Giăng" for John son of Zebedee
decisions.reason: Protestant forms, in line with the style guide's names; James is not in its list. John the apostle is "Giăng" as the Baptist is (style guide, section 4).

decisions.choice: Santiago
decisions.reason: The name most Spanish readers know for this apostle, as the Spanish of Galatians writes it for the Lord's brother.

source.text: καὶ ἀφέντες τὸν πατέρα αὐτῶν Ζεβεδαῖον ἐν τῷ πλοίῳ μετὰ τῶν μισθωτῶν ἀπῆλθον ὀπίσω αὐτοῦ.

records.literal_gloss: and having left the father of them Zebedee in the boat with the hired men they went away after him.

en.L: And leaving their father Zebedee in the boat with the hired men, they went away after {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}.
en.B: Leaving their father Zebedee in the boat with the hired workers, they went off after {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}.
en.R: They left their father Zebedee in the boat with the workers he paid, and they went with Jesus.

vi.L: Và bỏ cha mình là Xê-bê-đê ở lại trong thuyền với những người làm thuê, họ đi theo sau {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}}.
vi.B: Họ để cha mình là Xê-bê-đê lại trong thuyền với những người làm công, rồi đi theo {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}}.
vi.R: Họ để cha mình là Xê-bê-đê ở lại trong thuyền với những người làm công được ông trả lương, rồi đi theo Đức Giê-xu.

ko.L: 그러자 그들은 자기들의 아버지 세베대를 품꾼들과 함께 배에 남겨 두고, 그분의 뒤를 따라 떠나갔다.
ko.B: 그들은 아버지 세베대를 일꾼들과 함께 배에 남겨 두고 예수를 따라나섰다.
ko.R: 그들은 아버지 세베대를, 품삯을 받고 일하는 일꾼들과 함께 배에 두고 예수와 함께 떠났다.

es.L: Y dejando a su padre Zebedeo en la barca con los jornaleros, se fueron detrás de {{deity_pronoun:él|Él}}.
es.B: Dejaron a su padre Zebedeo en la barca con los trabajadores contratados y se fueron tras {{deity_pronoun:él|Él}}.
es.R: Dejaron a su padre Zebedeo en la barca con los trabajadores a los que él pagaba, y se fueron con Jesús.

fr.L: Et laissant leur père Zébédée dans la barque avec les ouvriers, ils s’en allèrent derrière {{deity_pronoun:lui|Lui}}.
fr.B: Laissant leur père Zébédée dans la barque avec les ouvriers qu’il employait, ils partirent à {{deity_pronoun:sa|Sa}} suite.
fr.R: Ils ont laissé leur père Zébédée dans le bateau avec les ouvriers qu’il payait, et ils sont partis avec Jésus.

decisions.choice: the hired men: Zebedee's paid workers
decisions.reason: Zebedee's fishing business had hired workers, so the sons did not leave their father alone, but they did leave a family business.

decisions.choice: went away after him: left to become his followers
alternatives: went on a short trip with him
decisions.reason: "After him" echoes "come after me" (1:17).

decisions.choice: went with Jesus
decisions.reason: Readable says plainly what following meant, and names Jesus.

decisions.choice: "품꾼" (L); "일꾼" (B); "품삯을 받고 일하는 일꾼" (R)
decisions.reason: The word means workers paid by the day (meaning decision). "품꾼" says exactly that; "삯꾼" has the negative sense of the hired man in John 10:12-13, which Mark does not intend here.

source.text: Καὶ εἰσπορεύονται εἰς Καφαρναούμ.

records.literal_gloss: And they go into Capernaum.

en.L: And they go into Capernaum.
en.B: They made their way to Capernaum.
en.R: Then they went to the town of Capernaum.

vi.L: Và họ vào Ca-bê-na-um.
vi.B: Họ đi đến Ca-bê-na-um.
vi.R: Rồi họ đến thị trấn Ca-bê-na-um.

ko.L: 그리고 그들이 가버나움으로 들어간다.
ko.B: 그들은 가버나움으로 갔다.
ko.R: 그런 다음 그들은 가버나움 마을로 갔다.

es.L: Y entran en Capernaúm.
es.B: Llegaron a Capernaúm.
es.R: Luego fueron al pueblo de Capernaúm.

fr.L: Et ils entrent dans Capharnaüm.
fr.B: Ils se rendirent à Capharnaüm.
fr.R: Ensuite, ils sont allés dans la ville de Capharnaüm.

decisions.choice: Capernaum: a fishing town on the north shore of the Sea of Galilee
decisions.reason: Capernaum became the base of Jesus' work in Galilee (2:1).

decisions.choice: they go: the present tense of storytelling
decisions.reason: Mark often tells past events in the present tense to make them vivid.

decisions.choice: go (L); made their way (B); went (R)
decisions.reason: Literal keeps Mark's present tense. Balanced and Readable use the past.

decisions.choice: Capernaúm
decisions.reason: The usual form in Spanish Protestant Bibles.

source.text: καὶ εὐθὺς τοῖς σάββασιν ἐδίδασκεν εἰς τὴν συναγωγήν.

records.literal_gloss: and immediately on the Sabbaths he was teaching into the synagogue.

en.L: And immediately on the Sabbath, [going] into the synagogue, {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} was teaching.
en.B: On the Sabbath {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} went straight into the synagogue and taught there.
en.R: On the Sabbath, the weekly day of rest, Jesus went into the synagogue, where the Jews met to worship, and taught the people.

vi.L: Và lập tức vào ngày Sa-bát, [đi] vào nhà hội, {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} giảng dạy.
vi.B: Vào ngày Sa-bát, {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} liền vào nhà hội và giảng dạy ở đó.
vi.R: Vào ngày Sa-bát, là ngày nghỉ hằng tuần, Đức Giê-xu đi vào nhà hội, nơi người Do Thái nhóm lại thờ phượng, và dạy dỗ dân chúng.

ko.L: 그리고 곧 안식일에 그분은 회당에 [들어가셔서] 가르치셨다.
ko.B: 안식일이 되자 예수께서 곧바로 회당에 들어가셔서 가르치셨다.
ko.R: 안식일, 곧 한 주에 한 번 쉬는 날에 예수께서 회당에 들어가셔서 사람들을 가르치셨다. 회당은 유대인들이 모여 하나님께 예배하는 곳이었다.

es.L: Y enseguida, el sábado, [entrando] en la sinagoga, enseñaba.
es.B: El sábado fue directamente a la sinagoga y se puso a enseñar.
es.R: El sábado, el día de descanso, Jesús fue a la sinagoga, el lugar donde los judíos se reunían para adorar a Dios, y enseñó a la gente.

fr.L: Et aussitôt, le sabbat, [étant entré] dans la synagogue, {{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} enseignait.
fr.B: Dès le jour du sabbat, {{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} entra dans la synagogue et se mit à enseigner.
fr.R: Le jour du sabbat, le jour de repos de chaque semaine, Jésus est entré dans la synagogue, la maison où les Juifs se réunissaient pour prier, et {{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} a enseigné les gens.

decisions.choice: on the Sabbaths: on the Sabbath day
decisions.reason: The plural is the normal way of naming the Sabbath day, like the Hebrew. One day is meant, as the story that follows shows.

decisions.choice: the SBLGNT has no verb for entering
decisions.reason: Many manuscripts read "having gone into the synagogue, he was teaching". The SBLGNT text has only "into the synagogue", which still implies that he went in. Reviewers should check this against the SBLGNT apparatus.

decisions.choice: the synagogue: the meeting place for prayer and reading the law
decisions.reason: Jews met in the synagogue on the Sabbath to pray and to hear the scriptures read and explained. A visiting teacher could be asked to speak.

decisions.choice: he was teaching: he taught, and kept on teaching
alternatives: he had been teaching for a long time
decisions.reason: The verb is continuous, setting the scene for what happened while he taught (1:23).

decisions.choice: the weekly day of rest; where the Jews met to worship
decisions.reason: Readable explains the two words for readers who do not know them.

decisions.choice: le sabbat, lowercase
decisions.reason: French writes the day with a small letter, as it does the days of the week, and as the French of John and Hebrews already does.

decisions.choice: Dès le jour du sabbat
decisions.reason: "Dès" carries Mark's "immediately" here: the first Sabbath in Capernaum, Jesus was already teaching.

source.text: καὶ ἐξεπλήσσοντο ἐπὶ τῇ διδαχῇ αὐτοῦ, ἦν γὰρ διδάσκων αὐτοὺς ὡς ἐξουσίαν ἔχων καὶ οὐχ ὡς οἱ γραμματεῖς.

records.literal_gloss: And they were astonished at the teaching of him; he was for teaching them as authority having and not as the scribes.

en.L: And they were astonished at {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} teaching, for {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} was teaching them as [one] having authority, and not as the scribes.
en.B: His teaching astounded them. Unlike the scribes, {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} taught them as someone who has authority.
en.R: The people were amazed at {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} teaching. He did not teach like the teachers of God's law. He taught like someone who had real authority.

vi.L: Và họ kinh ngạc về sự dạy dỗ của {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}}, vì {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} dạy họ như [người] có thẩm quyền, chứ không như các thầy thông giáo.
vi.B: Sự dạy dỗ của {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} khiến họ sửng sốt, vì {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} dạy họ như một người có thẩm quyền, không giống như các thầy thông giáo.
vi.R: Dân chúng rất ngạc nhiên về sự dạy dỗ của {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}}. Ngài không dạy như các thầy dạy luật của Đức Chúa Trời. Ngài dạy như một người có thẩm quyền thật sự.

ko.L: 그리고 사람들은 그분의 가르침에 크게 놀라고 있었다. 그분이 율법학자들과 같지 않고, 권위를 가진 [분]과 같이 그들을 가르치고 계셨기 때문이다.
ko.B: 사람들은 그분의 가르침에 깜짝 놀랐다. 그분은 율법학자들과 달리 권위 있는 분으로서 그들을 가르치셨기 때문이다.
ko.R: 사람들은 예수께서 가르치시는 것을 듣고 놀랐다. 예수께서는 율법 선생들과 다르게 가르치셨다. 참된 권위를 가진 분처럼 가르치셨다.

es.L: Y se asombraban de {{deity_pronoun:su|Su}} enseñanza, porque les enseñaba como [quien] tiene autoridad, y no como los escribas.
es.B: Su enseñanza los dejaba asombrados, porque les enseñaba como alguien que tiene autoridad, y no como los escribas.
es.R: La gente estaba asombrada de {{deity_pronoun:su|Su}} enseñanza. No enseñaba como los maestros de la ley de Dios. Enseñaba como alguien que tiene verdadera autoridad.

fr.L: Et ils étaient frappés de {{deity_pronoun:son|Son}} enseignement, car {{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} les enseignait comme [quelqu’un] ayant autorité, et non comme les scribes.
fr.B: Son enseignement les frappait d’étonnement, car {{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} les enseignait comme quelqu’un qui a autorité, et non comme les scribes.
fr.R: Les gens étaient très étonnés par {{deity_pronoun:son|Son}} enseignement. Jésus n’enseignait pas comme les spécialistes de la Loi. Il enseignait comme quelqu’un qui a une vraie autorité.

decisions.choice: astonished: struck with amazement
decisions.reason: The word means to be overwhelmed by something. It says nothing yet about whether they believed.

decisions.choice: authority: the right and the power to speak and act
decisions.reason: Jesus' authority is shown at once over an unclean spirit (1:27). His opponents later ask where his authority comes from (11:28).

decisions.choice: the scribes: experts in the law of Moses
decisions.reason: The scribes taught the law and how to keep it, often by quoting earlier teachers. They become Jesus' opponents (2:6; 3:22).

decisions.choice: the teachers of God's law
decisions.reason: Readable uses a name that says what the scribes did, as in Matthew 2:4.

decisions.choice: "thầy thông giáo" (L, B); "thầy dạy luật" (R) for the scribes
decisions.reason: As in John 8:3: the Protestant term at Literal and Balanced, and the plainer "teachers of the law" at Readable. "kinh sư" is the Catholic word. Used through Mark.

decisions.choice: "율법학자들" (L, B); "율법 선생들" (R), through Mark
decisions.reason: As John 8:3 in Korean: "서기관" is the traditional Protestant word but suggests a clerk to a modern reader; these men were experts who taught and applied the law of Moses (meaning decision).

decisions.choice: "권위" for authority in Jesus' teaching (1:22, 1:27)
decisions.reason: "권위" is the authority that makes a teacher's word carry weight, which is the contrast with the scribes here; "권세" is kept for the power to act in 2:10.

decisions.choice: escribas (L, B); maestros de la ley de Dios (R)
decisions.reason: As in John 8:3: "escribas" is the Spanish name for these experts in the law of Moses (meaning decision m3); Readable says what they did. Throughout Mark.

decisions.choice: les scribes (L, B); les spécialistes de la Loi (R), for the whole book
decisions.reason: As in John 8:3: "scribe" today suggests a copyist, so Readable says what they were (meaning decision m3). "Maîtres de la Loi" would clash with "Maître", the address to Jesus, and "docteurs" now means physicians.

source.text: καὶ εὐθὺς ἦν ἐν τῇ συναγωγῇ αὐτῶν ἄνθρωπος ἐν πνεύματι ἀκαθάρτῳ καὶ ἀνέκραξεν λέγων· Τί ἡμῖν καὶ σοί, Ἰησοῦ Ναζαρηνέ;

records.literal_gloss: And immediately there was in the synagogue of them a man in a spirit unclean, and he cried out \v 24 saying, What to us and to you, Jesus Nazarene?

en.L: And immediately there was in their synagogue a man with an unclean spirit, and he cried out, \v 24 saying, "What [is there] to us and to {{deity_pronoun:you|You}}, Jesus of Nazareth?
en.B: Right then, in their synagogue, there was a man with an unclean spirit, and he screamed, \v 24 "What do {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} have to do with us, Jesus of Nazareth?
en.R: Right then a man with an evil spirit in him was in the synagogue. He shouted, \v 24 "Jesus from Nazareth, why are {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} bothering us?

vi.L: Và lập tức trong nhà hội của họ có một người [bị] uế linh [ám], và người ấy kêu lên \v 24 rằng: "Giữa chúng tôi với ông có [liên quan] gì, Giê-xu người Na-xa-rét?
vi.B: Ngay lúc ấy, trong nhà hội của họ có một người bị uế linh ám, và người ấy hét lên: \v 24 "Giê-xu người Na-xa-rét, ông với chúng tôi có liên quan gì?
vi.R: Ngay lúc đó, trong nhà hội có một người bị tà linh nhập. Người ấy la lớn: \v 24 "Giê-xu người Na-xa-rét, sao ông lại quấy rầy chúng tôi?

ko.L: 그리고 곧 그들의 회당에 더러운 영에 [사로잡힌] 사람이 있었는데, 그가 소리를 지르며 \v 24 말했다. "우리와 당신에게 무슨 [상관이 있습니까], 나사렛 사람 예수여?
ko.B: 바로 그때 그들의 회당에 더러운 영이 들린 사람이 하나 있었는데, 그가 소리를 지르며 \v 24 말했다. "나사렛 예수여, 당신이 우리와 무슨 상관이 있습니까?
ko.R: 그때 회당에 악한 영이 들어가 있는 사람이 있었다. 그가 큰 소리로 외쳤다. \v 24 "나사렛 예수여, 왜 우리를 괴롭힙니까?

es.L: Y enseguida había en la sinagoga de ellos un hombre con un espíritu impuro, y gritó, \v 24 diciendo: «¿Qué [hay] para nosotros y para {{deity_pronoun:ti|Ti}}, Jesús nazareno?
es.B: En ese momento, en la sinagoga de ellos, había un hombre con un espíritu impuro, que se puso a gritar: \v 24 «¿Qué tienes que ver con nosotros, Jesús de Nazaret?
es.R: En ese momento estaba en la sinagoga un hombre que tenía dentro un espíritu malo. Gritó: \v 24 «Jesús de Nazaret, ¿por qué nos molestas?

decisions.choice: with an unclean spirit: in the power of an unclean spirit
alternatives: a man who had a bad attitude
decisions.reason: "In a spirit" means held under the spirit's power. The spirit speaks through the man.

decisions.choice: an unclean spirit: an evil spirit, a demon
decisions.reason: Mark calls these beings both unclean spirits and demons (1:34; 3:22, 30). "Unclean" sets them against the Holy Spirit (1:8) and the Holy One of God (1:24).

decisions.choice: what to us and to you: what do we have in common? leave us alone
alternatives: what do you want from us, a friendly question
decisions.reason: The phrase keeps someone at a distance (Judges 11:12; 1 Kings 17:18). Here it is hostile.

decisions.choice: us: the spirit speaks for all the unclean spirits
alternatives: the man and the spirit together
decisions.reason: The spirit speaks for its kind, which Jesus has come to defeat (3:27).

decisions.choice: an evil spirit
decisions.reason: Readable says "evil", since "unclean" suggests dirt to new readers.

decisions.choice: "uế linh" (L, B); "tà linh" (R) for the unclean spirit
decisions.reason: "uế linh" says "unclean spirit" in one word; Readable uses the plainer "tà linh" (evil spirit), as the English Readable does. "quỷ" is kept for "demon" (1:32-39). Used through Mark.

decisions.choice: the spirit says "Giê-xu" without "Đức", "ông" for "you" and "chúng tôi" for itself
decisions.reason: A hostile speaker does not honour Jesus, as the arresting party in John 18:5; "ông" is the word for a man one does not honour, and words of address take no deity_pronoun span.

decisions.choice: "더러운 영" (L, B), "악한 영" (R), through Mark; "더러운 영에 [사로잡힌]" (L), "영이 들린" (B)
decisions.reason: "영" keeps Mark's word "spirit" and "더러운" keeps "unclean"; "귀신" is kept for the Greek word for demon (1:32-39). Readable says "악한 영", as the English Readable says "evil spirit". Literal brackets the verb Korean needs for "in a spirit" (in its power, meaning decision); Balanced uses the idiom "들리다" (be possessed).

decisions.choice: the unclean spirit speaks to Jesus in 합쇼체, with "당신" and no honorific -시- for him
decisions.reason: The style guide gives 합쇼체 for those who speak to Jesus and allows 해라체 for open opponents. The spirit both resists Jesus and fears him; formal endings with the cool "당신" and no honorific -시- keep that distance, as the envoys' questioning does in John 1:19-25. A reviewer should settle this for all of Mark (also 3:11, 5:7).

decisions.choice: espíritu impuro (L, B); espíritu malo (R)
decisions.reason: "Impuro" keeps the Greek word's sense of being unfit for God's presence (meaning decision m2); "inmundo" is the traditional word but now sounds like dirt. Readable says "malo", as the English says "evil". Throughout Mark.

decisions.choice: un esprit impur (L, B); un esprit mauvais (R), for the whole book
decisions.reason: "Impur" is the plain modern word for the Greek adjective, unclean in the sense of the law; "immonde" is old-fashioned. Readable says what such a spirit is, as the English Readable does (meaning decision m2).

decisions.choice: sous [l’emprise d’] (L); Quoi [de commun entre] nous et toi (L); Que nous veux-tu ? (B)
decisions.reason: French needs words the Greek leaves out to say "in [the power of] a spirit" (meaning decision m1) and "what to us and to you"; Literal brackets them. Balanced uses the French idiom "Que nous veux-tu ?", which carries the hostile "leave us alone" of the Greek (meaning decision m3).

en.B: Are {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} here to destroy us?
en.R: Have {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} come to get rid of us?

decisions.choice: a question, as the SBLGNT prints it

decisions.reason: The earliest manuscripts have no question marks, and the words can be read either way. The question fits the alarm of the other questions around it.

decisions.choice: destroy: the end of the evil spirits' power

en.R: I know who {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} are. You are God's Holy One!"

es.R: Yo sé quién eres. ¡Eres el Santo de Dios!».

fr.B: Je sais qui {{deity_pronoun:tu|Tu}} es : le Saint de Dieu ! »

decisions.choice: the Holy One of God: the one set apart and belonging to God
decisions.reason: The spirit, unclean, names Jesus as the one who is holy, belonging wholly to God (compare John 6:69).

decisions.choice: I know who you are: naming him to resist him
decisions.reason: Knowing and saying another's name was thought to give power over him. Jesus silences the spirit (1:25).

decisions.choice: "하나님의 거룩한 분"
decisions.reason: The title names Jesus as set apart and belonging to God (meaning decision); "분" is the respectful noun the title calls for even in the spirit's mouth, while "자" is old-fashioned and now slightly disparaging.

decisions.choice: Te conozco, [sé] quién eres
decisions.reason: The Greek says "I know you, who you are"; Spanish cannot hang the question on "conocer", so Literal supplies the verb "saber". "Te" opens the sentence and is written plain.

decisions.choice: Je te connais, [je sais] qui tu es
decisions.reason: The Greek says "I know you, who you are"; French cannot hang the question on "connaître", so Literal brackets the second verb.

source.text: καὶ ἐπετίμησεν αὐτῷ ὁ Ἰησοῦς λέγων· Φιμώθητι καὶ ἔξελθε ἐξ αὐτοῦ.

records.literal_gloss: And rebuked him the Jesus saying, Be silenced and come out of him.

en.L: And Jesus rebuked him, saying, "Be silenced, and come out of him!"
en.B: Jesus ordered it sternly, "Silence! Come out of the man!"
en.R: Jesus spoke strongly to the evil spirit. He said, "Be quiet! Come out of the man!"

vi.L: Và Đức Giê-xu quở trách nó, nói rằng: "Hãy im đi, và ra khỏi người này!"
vi.B: Đức Giê-xu nghiêm khắc ra lệnh cho nó: "Im đi! Hãy ra khỏi người này!"
vi.R: Đức Giê-xu nói mạnh mẽ với tà linh: "Im đi! Ra khỏi người này!"

ko.L: 그러자 예수께서 그를 꾸짖으시며 말씀하셨다. "입을 다물고 그에게서 나와라!"

es.L: Y Jesús lo reprendió, diciendo: «¡Enmudece, y sal de él!».
es.B: Jesús le dio una orden tajante: «¡Silencio! ¡Sal de este hombre!».
es.R: Jesús le habló con dureza al espíritu malo. Le dijo: «¡Cállate! ¡Sal de este hombre!».

fr.L: Et Jésus le reprit sévèrement, disant : « Tais-toi, et sors de lui ! »
fr.B: Jésus lui donna un ordre sévère : « Silence ! Sors de cet homme ! »
fr.R: Jésus a parlé durement à l’esprit mauvais. Il a dit : « Tais-toi ! Sors de cet homme ! »

decisions.choice: rebuked: gave a stern command
decisions.reason: The word is used for Jesus' commands to spirits (3:12) and to the wind and sea (4:39). It is a word of power.

decisions.choice: be silenced: be muzzled, stop speaking
decisions.reason: The verb means to muzzle. Jesus will not let the spirit name him (1:34).

decisions.choice: him: the spirit is addressed; the man is the one it leaves
decisions.reason: Jesus speaks to the spirit and orders it out of the man.

decisions.choice: it; the man (B, R)
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable say "it" for the spirit and "the man" for the one it is in, so that the two are not confused.

decisions.choice: "nó" for the spirit; commands with no pronoun; "người này" for the man
decisions.reason: The narrator speaks of the spirit as "nó", as of a thing without honour; Jesus' commands need no pronoun, so neither the archaic "ngươi" nor a choice of relation is forced.

decisions.choice: "입을 다물어라" (L, R), "조용히 하여라" (B)
decisions.reason: The Greek means "be muzzled" (meaning decision); "입을 다물다" keeps the picture of the mouth shut. "잠잠하라" is the older Bible form.

decisions.choice: enmudece
decisions.reason: The Greek verb is passive, "be muzzled" (meaning decision m2); "enmudecer" keeps the sense of being silenced better than the everyday "cállate".

decisions.choice: le reprit ... sors de lui (L)
decisions.reason: French "esprit" is masculine, so Literal's "le" and "lui" can stand, like the Greek, for the spirit and for the man (meaning decision m3); Balanced and Readable name the man.

source.text: καὶ σπαράξαν αὐτὸν τὸ πνεῦμα τὸ ἀκάθαρτον καὶ φωνῆσαν φωνῇ μεγάλῃ ἐξῆλθεν ἐξ αὐτοῦ.

ko.R: 악한 영은 그 사람을 마구 뒤흔들었다. 그러고는 크게 소리를 지르며 그에게서 나왔다.

es.L: Y el espíritu impuro, sacudiéndolo con violencia y gritando a gran voz, salió de él.
es.B: El espíritu impuro sacudió al hombre con convulsiones, dio un fuerte alarido y salió de él.
es.R: El espíritu malo hizo que el hombre se sacudiera con fuerza. Luego dio un grito muy fuerte y salió de él.

fr.L: Et l’esprit impur, l’ayant secoué de convulsions et ayant crié d’une voix forte, sortit de lui.
fr.B: L’esprit impur secoua l’homme avec violence, poussa un grand cri et sortit de lui.
fr.R: L’esprit mauvais a secoué l’homme très fort. Puis il a poussé un grand cri et il est sorti de lui.

decisions.choice: throwing into convulsions: shaking him violently
decisions.reason: The word describes a violent fit (9:26). The man is not harmed in the end.

decisions.choice: crying out: the spirit's last protest as it obeys
decisions.reason: The spirit cries out but has to leave, which the crowd notices (1:27).

es.B: Todos quedaron asombrados y comentaban entre ellos: «¿Qué es esto?
es.R: Toda la gente estaba asombrada. Se preguntaban unos a otros: «¿Qué está pasando?

fr.B: Tous furent saisis de stupeur et se mirent à discuter entre eux : « Qu’est-ce que cela ?
fr.R: Tout le monde était très étonné. Les gens se demandaient les uns aux autres : « Qu’est-ce qui se passe ?

decisions.choice: amazed: astonished, close to alarm
decisions.reason: The word is stronger than the one in 1:22 and has a sense of awe and fear.

decisions.choice: questioned among themselves: discussed and argued
decisions.reason: They talk it over with each other, trying to understand what they saw.

decisions.choice: the people speak among themselves in 해라체
decisions.reason: Between equals in a crowd the plain style is the default (style guide, section 4).

source.text: διδαχὴ καινή· κατ’ ἐξουσίαν καὶ τοῖς πνεύμασι τοῖς ἀκαθάρτοις ἐπιτάσσει, καὶ ὑπακούουσιν αὐτῷ.

records.literal_gloss: A teaching new with authority; even the spirits the unclean he commands, and they obey him.

en.R: This man teaches something new, and {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} teaches with authority! He even tells evil spirits what to do, and they obey {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}!"

vi.L: Một sự dạy dỗ mới, với thẩm quyền! Ngay cả các uế linh ông ấy cũng ra lệnh, và chúng vâng lời ông ấy."

es.L: ¡Una enseñanza nueva con autoridad! Incluso a los espíritus impuros manda, y {{deity_pronoun:le|Le}} obedecen».
es.B: ¡Una enseñanza nueva, y con autoridad! Da órdenes hasta a los espíritus impuros, y ellos {{deity_pronoun:le|Le}} obedecen».
es.R: Este hombre enseña algo nuevo, ¡y lo enseña con autoridad! Hasta les da órdenes a los espíritus malos, y ellos {{deity_pronoun:le|Le}} obedecen».

fr.L: Un enseignement nouveau, avec autorité ! Même aux esprits impurs {{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} commande, et ils {{deity_pronoun:lui|Lui}} obéissent. »
fr.B: Voilà un enseignement nouveau, donné avec autorité ! Il commande même aux esprits impurs, et ils {{deity_pronoun:lui|Lui}} obéissent ! »
fr.R: Cet homme enseigne quelque chose de nouveau, et {{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} enseigne avec autorité ! Il donne même des ordres aux esprits mauvais, et ils {{deity_pronoun:lui|Lui}} obéissent ! »

decisions.choice: with authority goes with the new teaching
alternatives: with authority he commands even the unclean spirits
decisions.reason: The SBLGNT puts a break after "with authority", so the phrase describes the teaching. With the break before it, it describes the commands. Either way Jesus' word has authority.

decisions.choice: new: new in kind, not only recent
decisions.reason: The word means fresh or of a new kind. Teaching that drives out spirits by a word is something the people have not met before.

decisions.choice: even unclean spirits obey him: his word has God's power
decisions.reason: Jesus uses no ritual or name, only a command, and the spirits must obey.

decisions.choice: the crowd speaks of Jesus as "ông ấy", with no setting span
decisions.reason: The people do not yet know who he is; they speak of him as of a respected man, as the people in John 9:11-12 do. The narrator's "Ngài" stays for the narrator.

decisions.choice: the astonished people speak of Jesus with the honorific ("그분", "이분", "명령하시고")
decisions.reason: They are struck with awe at his authority, and a Korean speaker in awe refers to the person respectfully; the scribes in 2:6-7 and 2:16, who disapprove, speak of him without the honorific.
